papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. As a toolkit, KD spans soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate representation matching, layer- or module-level mapping, progressive replacement strategies, and online or multi-teacher regimes. KD yields large gains in memory, latency, and energy efficiency while often retaining most of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation strategies, and attention to robustness and privacy. Practitioners should treat KD as a central element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, and careful evaluation—rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original model's utility. Empirical results across vision, language, recommendation, and generation tasks show that carefully designed distillation—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate feature and relational transfer, online co-training, and progressive module replacement—enables large reductions in latency and memory with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and augmentation, and targeted mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, and privacy leakage. Treating KD as a system-level primitive and combining it with complementary compression and data strategies yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a reliable and versatile technique for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when combined with architecture-aware design, layer- and representation-level alignment, and appropriate data strategies. However, its success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle distributional or data-availability gaps; KD therefore belongs at the center of compression pipelines rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When used as a system-level strategy—choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely delivers favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory in vision and language tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: data availability, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, and robustness or fairness concerns limit what a distilled student can inherit reliably. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the default first-line method within a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, data strategies (including data-free or privacy-aware approaches), and explicit evaluation for rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, system-level approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides flexible transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and student pretraining. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to manage data access, domain shift, and privacy. When KD is applied as part of a considered pipeline that includes representation-aware objectives, targeted data strategies (including data-free synthesis when needed), and privacy-aware mechanisms, it delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs while exposing predictable limits that practitioners can mitigate.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Foundation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible path to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Through a variety of transfer targets and training schedules, KD enables major reductions in parameter count, memory use, and latency while often preserving most of a teacher’s task performance. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student pre-training and capacity, availability or synthesis of data, and complementary compression steps. KD is best treated as a toolkit to be combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a primary, flexible strategy for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD supports a wide range of supervision signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses), training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, adversarial, data-free), and combinations with structural compression (pruning, quantization) or architecture search. When applied with task- and student-aware design choices, KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs; however, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, capacity alignment, and careful selection of what to transfer. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as the backbone of compression while integrating complementary methods and safeguards to address gaps in robustness, privacy, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Strategy Path to Compressing Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep models while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and deployment settings, KD enables smaller models to inherit predictive behavior, internal structure, and cross-model insights from larger teachers. Best results arise when distillation is combined with complementary strategies — internal representation matching, curriculum scheduling, multi-teacher selection, data augmentation, meta-learned teachers, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols — yielding compact, efficient, and robust student models suitable for edge, federated, and low-precision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques that transfer information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. KD methods differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and how training proceeds (offline teacher supervision, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, or data-free synthesis). Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific choices. Empirical evidence shows KD reliably yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, but success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signals, and constraints such as access to original training data or deployment hardware.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multifaceted approach for shrinking large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD operates through multiple channels — softened outputs, intermediate-representation matching, contrastive or relational signals, and self- or multi-teacher schedules — and composes effectively with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. When designed as a system-level primitive that accounts for teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and deployment constraints, distillation yields substantial practical gains in latency, memory, and energy use. Nonetheless, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of robustness, rare behaviors, and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD mechanisms — soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and task- or deployment-aware pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in inference cost, but success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and task-specific considerations (e.g., preserving fine-grained sequence behavior or relational structure). Privacy, heterogeneity of deployment devices, and data-scarce regimes motivate variants with differential privacy, few-shot or cross-layer schemes, and heterogeneous multi-model sharing to ensure inclusive and practical compression.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. Over the past decade KD has diversified from soft-label (logit) matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, attention and relational supervision, contrastive and projector-based objectives, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture co-design) and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in inference cost with modest losses in task performance. Realizing these benefits in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and availability, and evaluation for robustness and fairness; several open problems remain, notably reliable data-free distillation, principled teacher design, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD strategies vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate representations, relations), how it is transferred (logit matching, feature-mimicking, projector layers, contrastive objectives, adversarial losses), and in deployment settings (data-available, data-free, federated or distributed, and online). Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance while enabling practical gains in speed and memory; however, method choice, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional shifts materially affect outcomes, and open problems remain in preserving rare-token behavior, transferring robustness and fairness, and compressing across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic training trick into a unifying framework for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and language tasks. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus from larger teachers to smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while largely preserving accuracy. Beyond plain size reduction, KD adapts to constraints that arise in real deployments — limited data or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogeneous architectures, and modality gaps — through techniques such as feature-level alignment, selective sampling, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, and data-free synthesis. As a practical bridge between research-scale architectures and deployable systems, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and serves both as an efficiency accelerator and as a lever for robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a unifying, practical framework to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while addressing concerns of computation, privacy, robustness, and limited task data. KD techniques span from logits- and feature-based matching to progressive module replacement, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free (zero-shot) synthesis, and federated output-sharing, and when combined with careful data augmentation and generative replay they yield compact models that retain much of the teacher utility in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD has proven effective across modalities and tasks, enabling multimodal generation, compact evaluation metrics, and efficient inference. However, KD is not a black-box cure: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, intermediate layers), how teachers and students are paired or trained, and on optimization and regularization choices. I argue that KD should be viewed as a flexible toolkit—comprising feature-level mimicking, layer-aware projection, self- and teacher-free variants, and teacher-adaptation strategies—applied with careful attention to teacher-student interaction and training dynamics to achieve reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has developed a broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and feature-level transfer, multi‑teacher and online schemes, and data‑free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data strategies, and optimization choices are carefully managed. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and fairness under compression, and operating under limited or no access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade a diverse family of distillation methods has emerged—logit-level soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, multi-teacher ensembles, and privacy-aware adaptations—applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data availability and domain mismatch; combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture search, quantization) and task-aware pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Principled Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive power. KD is most effective when it goes beyond naïve soft-label copying: matching internal representations, aligning inputs and tokenization, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and adapting teacher updates or curricula all materially affect transfer quality. KD should be used as part of a broader compression pipeline (architecture design, quantization, pruning, or data strategies) and with explicit checks for rare-token behavior, fairness, and robustness. When applied with these considerations, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for production constraints in vision, language, and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. It encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- or module-level mappings, and training-time adaptations that account for student capacity and deployment constraints. In practice KD is combined with complementary methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis) to meet latency, memory, or privacy requirements. KD is effective across vision, language, generative models, and view- or modality-specific tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, available data, and careful choice of distillation objectives and schedules; open challenges remain in robustness, rare-token behavior, fairness, and theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a pragmatic and flexible approach to compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in size and compute while retaining much of a teacher model's performance, and it adapts well to modalities from vision to speech and to task-specific constraints in NLP. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, mismatches between teacher and student, and the potential for poorer outcomes when distilling inappropriate teacher signals require careful method selection and evaluation. Best practice therefore combines tailored distillation architectures, curriculum or multi-teacher strategies, privacy-aware mechanisms where needed, and awareness of when label-smoothing or teacher-free alternatives are preferable.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in constrained environments. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and structural inductive biases; it supports multi-teacher, progressive, adversarial, and data-constrained variants; and it can be combined with architecture-aware design and data strategies to improve efficiency, robustness, and domain adaptability. While highly effective in practice, KD's success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and the availability and suitability of data, so it should be treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches to Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed diverse strategies—teacher–student logits matching, layer-wise representation matching, adversarial sample generation, progressive module replacement, many-to-many layer mapping, and task-aware filtering—to address capacity gaps, data access limits, privacy constraints, and robustness needs. Practical deployments additionally combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and federated protocols to meet hardware and communication budgets. Empirical work shows that careful design of distillation objectives and inputs can preserve most of the teacher’s accuracy and even transfer properties such as adversarial robustness, while specialized schemes enable distillation without original training data or across continual/heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has matured from simple logits-matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes soft-target supervision, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relation matching, data synthesis for data-free scenarios, online and federated distillation, and self-distillation. Empirical results show distilled students often approach teacher performance while yielding substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployability; however, practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy leakage. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative variants, theoretical insights, practical strategies, and open challenges to guide research and deployments in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision and NLP, KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with careful choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. However, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data availability, and deployment constraints determine whether distilled students approach teacher performance or inherit undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving or even improving generalization. The field combines a variety of approaches — from logit-level transfer to feature- and attention-level imitation, from data-free synthesis to multi-teacher ensembles and task-adaptive architecture search — and is applied across domains including NLP, vision, speech and healthcare. Contemporary work integrates distillation with pruning, neural architecture search, federated and privacy-preserving training, and meta-learning for better teacher-student alignment. Empirical results show substantial compression and speedups with modest accuracy loss when distillation is combined with architecture-aware optimization and data- or task-aware strategies. Ongoing challenges include handling imperfect teachers, distribution shift of synthetic data, privacy constraints, and transferring inductive biases across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across NLP, speech, vision, and recommendation systems, KD reduces inference cost and memory, enables deployment on constrained devices, and can transfer specialized capabilities when paired with appropriate data and training choices. Its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals), the availability and synthesis of training data, and teacher–student design; complementary compression tools and safeguards addressing bias, privacy, and distributional mismatch are often required for robust, real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compress large neural models for deployment, while preserving performance and enabling new capabilities such as efficient federated learning, data-free compression, interpretability, and few-shot adaptation. Across architectures and tasks, KD variants—ranging from layer-to-layer alignment and progressive module replacement to meta-learned teachers and adversarial data synthesis—provide methods to trade computation, memory, and communication for small changes in accuracy. These methods make it possible to bring large pretrained models into production and edge settings, and to reconcile competing requirements such as privacy, heterogeneity, and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving predictive performance. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, and data-centered strategies including augmentation and data-free synthesis. When combined with architecture-aware design, pretraining, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and edge settings. However, its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, optimization dynamics, and practical concerns such as privacy, robustness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used approach to compressing large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods span soft-logit matching, ensemble distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and privacy- or data-aware variants. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show that carefully chosen distillation targets and student–teacher alignment can achieve large reductions in inference cost with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in performance. However, practical success depends on capacity-matching, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, degraded rare-token behavior in NLP, and privacy concerns. KD performs best as a component of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture choices, pruning/quantization, and data-centric strategies.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Multifaceted, and Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and by integrating with data strategies and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and evaluation of rare-token, robustness, and fairness behaviors. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core design paradigm that is adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints and paired with complementary methods and targeted evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple logit matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data- and communication-constrained protocols, and progressive module replacement. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and training protocols. Important open issues include robust transfer under distribution shift, efficient distillation when teacher cost is high, and preserving fairness and safety properties in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become practical tools to reduce model size and computation while retaining much of the performance of large teachers. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, approaches include transferring soft logits, mimicking internal features or attention maps, layering/structural adaptations, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-preserving methods. Empirical results demonstrate that careful distillation can yield compact students that approach teacher accuracy and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, but open challenges remain in robustness, task-specific distillation design, and distributed training dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied model compression technique that trains a compact student model to emulate a larger teacher (or ensemble) so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD has been adapted across domains (vision, graphs, NLP, multimodal systems) and combined with other compression methods; it can transfer logits, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge, and it can be extended to multi-teacher, self-distillation, and privacy-aware settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves generalization but also reveals limits and failure modes that motivate augmented objectives, data strategies, and teacher-training methods to achieve more effective, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining as much task performance as possible. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a broad set of practical techniques that include intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, online and multi-teacher training, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially shrink model size and latency for vision and language systems and can be adapted for privacy-sensitive and distributed settings; however, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data, and it faces open challenges in robustness, cross-domain generalization, and heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, and generation tasks. Contemporary KD methods extend far beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, curriculum and online schemes, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and tight integrations with architecture-level compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on matched teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data alternatives, and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-class behaviors. Open challenges remain in domain-shift robustness, privacy-sensitive distillation, automated student architecture design, and principled selection of which aspects of teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Compressing and Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, storage, and privacy constraints. By transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, KD enables large pre-trained NLP models to be adapted, accelerated, and sometimes even improved for downstream tasks and specific domains. Effective KD requires careful design choices—how to match intermediate layers, whether to rely on data or synthesize surrogates, how to combine multiple teachers, and how to account for fairness and domain shift. When combined with complementary compression techniques, KD becomes a core component of production-ready model compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened logits to a broad family of methods that include intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, data-free or synthetic-data strategies, and architecture-aware compression. Practically, KD enables favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks but requires careful design around the form of knowledge transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability and augmentation, and evaluation for robustness and undesired behavior. Open problems remain in reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in sequence tasks, and ensuring fairness and robustness in deployed compact models.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, system-level family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. Over the past decade KD has diversified from simple softened-logit matching into many practical recipes — intermediate-feature and attention matching, relation-aware losses, multi-teacher schemes, online or co-distillation, and data-free or federated variants — and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, compact pretraining) and task- or data-aware strategies. Empirical and analytic work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance and sometimes improve generalization, but outcomes depend critically on what knowledge is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and optimization dynamics; open challenges remain around robustness, rare-token and long-tail behavior, privacy, and principled student design.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a unified, pragmatic pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, augmenting or synthesizing data when necessary, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD consistently yields large efficiency gains (memory, compute, latency) while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and robustness concerns, and practical pipelines must address these limits through curriculum design, data-aware augmentation, and careful choice of distillation targets.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD encompasses a range of transferred signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational patterns, and ensemble outputs), operates under multiple training regimes (offline, online, multi‑teacher, and data‑free), and composes naturally with structural compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, speech, and language shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and attention to robustness, rare-token preservation, and fairness. Open challenges include reliable data‑free distillation, principled signal selection for heterogeneous architectures, and preserving safety‑critical behaviours under compression.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms (soft-targets, intermediate representation matching, relational and attention-based transfers, and data-side interventions) and is most effective when treated as a toolkit combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on teacher quality, data availability (including data-free or synthetic strategies), teacher–student capacity alignment, and robustness considerations. A principled KD practice adapts the transfer signals to task and data regimes, uses multi-teacher or data-synthesis techniques when needed, and explicitly pairs distillation with deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-Strategy Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—combining logits transfer, intermediate representation matching, teacher optimization, and data strategies—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student design, the availability and nature of data, robustness and fairness considerations, and the distillation objectives chosen. Best outcomes come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture choices, augmentation or data-synthesis techniques, and explicit attention to transfer limits.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has developed a broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and feature-level transfer, multi‑teacher and online schemes, and data‑free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data strategies, and optimization choices are carefully managed. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and fairness under compression, and operating under limited or no access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Compression Strategy for Practical Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the first-line strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations, is broadly applicable across modalities, and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is not a silver bullet — its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability, and how knowledge is represented and aligned — so production pipelines should combine KD with representation-aware objectives, student pretraining, and targeted data strategies to mitigate distributional and optimization pitfalls. When applied with these caveats, KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs that make large pretrained models practical for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Dependent Core for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and provenance, and explicit strategies to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or failing on low-frequency phenomena. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a central tool within an integrated compression strategy, tuned to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains compact student models to mimic larger teachers so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, practitioners match teacher output distributions, align intermediate representations, synthesize or filter data for student training, and combine distillation with structural compression (pruning, architecture search) to reach deployment targets. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher accuracy and sometimes improve generalization, but outcomes depend on the distillation signal, data provenance, student capacity, and training protocol. Practical deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to present supervision, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques.
