papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central Tool for Practical Model Compression, with Limits and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When combined with complementary strategies—such as intermediate-feature alignment, architecture-aware design, data-aware selection, and data-free synthesis—distillation enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. However, KD is not universally sufficient: careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch is required to avoid propagating errors or losing robustness.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a central, practical toolkit for compressing large models and transferring behavior from high-capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative modeling, practitioners combine soft-label supervision, intermediate-representation matching, data- and privacy-aware strategies, and architecture-aware choices to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. KD is effective when paired with complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, synthetic-data generation, curriculum schedules), but its success depends critically on what form of knowledge is distilled, how data or augmentations are used, and how teacher–student capacity and domain mismatches are managed. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, mitigating bias transfer, and firm theoretical characterizations that predict when and how distillation will work in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices for what and how to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), and when combined with complementary compression strategies (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Practical compression pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core tool whose design must be tailored to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-Line, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, practical starting point for compressing large models because it provides flexible, task‑aware mechanisms to transfer behavior from high-capacity teachers to efficient students. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute when combined with targeted design choices. However, its success depends on what signals are distilled, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and domain constraints; therefore KD must be integrated into a broader, context‑adapted compression pipeline rather than used as a blind one‑size‑fits‑all fix.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when its objectives, training dynamics, and data strategies are co‑designed with student architectures and deployment constraints. However, distillation is context‑dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, optimization dynamics, and explicit handling of rare or safety‑critical behaviors. Consequently, KD should be used as a default first‑line tool within integrated compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design) and applied with targeted diagnostics and mitigation steps for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that high-performing systems can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; they can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-design choices to meet hardware and application requirements. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can improve student generalization, but outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or federated settings), and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a flexible component in a broader compression strategy and adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and student architectures to the target deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across NLP, speech, vision, and recommendation systems, KD reduces inference cost and memory, enables deployment on constrained devices, and can transfer specialized capabilities when paired with appropriate data and training choices. Its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals), the availability and synthesis of training data, and teacher–student design; complementary compression tools and safeguards addressing bias, privacy, and distributional mismatch are often required for robust, real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. A spectrum of KD strategies has been developed—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, self-distillation, and data-free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows well-designed distillation pipelines can recover much of a teacher’s performance while delivering large gains in latency and memory, but outcomes depend on the choice of distillation signal, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints such as domain shift and privacy. Current practical directions emphasize representation-aware objectives, layer-alignment techniques, and hybrid pipelines that treat KD as a core element of system-level compression.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic family of techniques for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable ones. When treated as a system‑level design choice rather than a single loss term, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher's predictive power. Realizing these benefits in practice requires choosing what knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining KD with complementary practices such as compact pre‑training, data augmentation, or privacy‑aware data synthesis. KD is powerful but not universal: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher quality, and deployment constraints, so practitioners must evaluate and adapt distillation strategies to their task and context.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Evidence for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables deployment of high-performing but large neural models by training compact student models that mimic larger teachers. Empirical work across speech, NLP, vision, and federated settings shows KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving accuracy, and its effectiveness increases when combined with complementary techniques: pre-training compact architectures, adaptive layer mapping for transformers, data-centric augmentations, ensemble teachers, and robustness-aware objectives. This paper synthesizes results from recent studies to argue that a principled KD pipeline—pre-train compact students, match representations flexibly, leverage data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and incorporate robustness or task-specific objectives—yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and performance for practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad set of practical recipes—including logit (soft-target) supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and joint use with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—enable deployment of compact models across vision, language, and graph tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while reducing compute and memory, but effectiveness depends on the choice of transfer target, availability or synthesis of suitable data, student architecture, and training dynamics. Key open issues remain around principled explanations for when distillation helps, reliably transferring robustness and fairness properties, privacy-aware distillation, and automating student design for specific resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Poole
papers_seen.title: Position: Treat Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, Combined with Complementary Tools
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller students that can meet deployment constraints. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations—and when combined with architecture-aware techniques (pruning, quantization, or compact pretraining) it routinely produces deployable models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a single turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, the availability and provenance of distillation data, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Therefore KD should be the central element of compression pipelines, but applied as part of a hybrid, task-aware strategy that addresses representation mapping, data limitations, and downstream risks.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Across vision, speech, reinforcement learning, and NLP, KD has been adapted into logit-level supervision, intermediate feature and layer-wise matching, data augmentation strategies, data-free setups, and training-time architectural replacement. Recent work has expanded KD to address practical constraints—privacy in federated settings, bias mitigation in language models, low-precision deployment, and multi-task transfer—while also proposing task-aware and capacity-aware methods to reduce redundant or harmful teacher signals. This synthesis summarizes the mechanisms, extensions, strengths, and limitations documented in contemporary studies and highlights promising directions for making distilled models both efficient and robust.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary practices—such as pretraining compact students, representation-level matching, curriculum scheduling, teacher ensembles, and data augmentation—KD yields strong tradeoffs between efficiency and performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch; KD therefore functions best as a central, flexible component within a broader compression pipeline rather than as a one-size-fits-all cure.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining as much task performance as possible. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a broad set of practical techniques that include intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, online and multi-teacher training, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially shrink model size and latency for vision and language systems and can be adapted for privacy-sensitive and distributed settings; however, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data, and it faces open challenges in robustness, cross-domain generalization, and heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that the students retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when original data are unavailable, and deploying progressive or ensemble-based strategies. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search) and training-time strategies (curricula, online distillation, or federated protocols) to balance efficiency and accuracy. Despite strong empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and designing principled objectives and curricula that preserve robustness and task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, System‑Level Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. Treated as a system-level strategy—one that selects what knowledge to transfer, aligns teacher and student capacity, and composes with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies)—KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for many practical applications. However, its success is conditional: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns constrain outcomes, so KD must be applied thoughtfully and evaluated across deployment metrics.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Compact, Robust, and Adaptable Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers while enabling domain adaptation, deployment under resource constraints, privacy-preserving releases, and improved robustness. KD techniques span transfer from full teacher ensembles to single students, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation, and even data-free distillation; each variant addresses different operational constraints. However, distillation also carries risks (e.g., transfer of undesirable biases) and requires careful design choices (e.g., what information to transfer and what data to use). Combining advances across these variants yields effective, small NLP models fit for real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search — KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, data availability (including data‑free or privacy‑constrained scenarios), and careful design around teacher–student mismatch and task-specific objectives. Responsible, task-aware application of KD, integrated into system-level compression pipelines, produces the most reliable operational outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses soft-target matching, representation- and attention-level imitation, relational or contrastive signals, and multi-teacher or progressive schedules; it is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows that when distillation choices (what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and what data to use) are matched to student capacity and task requirements, distilled models can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing compute, memory, and latency, enabling practical on-device and low-latency NLP systems. Open challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token behaviors and robustness, and designing distillation strategies that explicitly account for deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi-Strategy Path for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for producing compact models that preserve much of larger models' performance. When treated as a flexible toolkit—integrating soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or low-precision numerics—KD enables deployable, efficient models across domains. KD is empirically effective but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or encountering optimization limits; best results arise from task- and data-aware distillation regimes and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks KD variants—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention patterns, multi-teacher and progressive schemes, and self-distillation—have enabled compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success typically requires co-design of the distillation signal, student architecture, data and augmentation choices, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization or pruning). Persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, handling limited or private data, preserving rare-token and robustness properties, and automating trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary practices—such as pretraining compact students, representation-level matching, curriculum scheduling, teacher ensembles, and data augmentation—KD yields strong tradeoffs between efficiency and performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch; KD therefore functions best as a central, flexible component within a broader compression pipeline rather than as a one-size-fits-all cure.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, transferring intermediate representations or attentions, leveraging ensembles or self-teaching, and operating in constrained settings via data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Across vision, generative models, and natural language tasks, distillation is used both as a standalone compression technique and as a complement to pruning and quantization. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability, and how to mitigate optimization and distributional mismatches. While KD often produces compact models that approach teacher performance, practical deployment requires careful design to avoid failure modes arising from heterogeneous data, limited student capacity, or misaligned training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Core, Proven Benefits, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what is transferred (logits, features, attention maps, or relations), how teachers and students are co-designed, and how data and deployment constraints are handled, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, and explicit treatment of robustness and privacy. Practical pipelines therefore combine KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and robustness/privacy objectives to produce compact models suitable for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students that preserve most of the teacher’s capability. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single loss function, KD supports multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), and it interoperates with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization) and data strategies (data-free synthesis, synthetic/distilled training sets). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, and explicit choices about what to transfer and how to align representations. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as a first-line method while designing task- and deployment-aware distillation pipelines and monitoring known failure modes such as teacher error propagation, low-frequency token degradation, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label transfers to a rich family of techniques including internal representation matching, attention- and channel-guided supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble signals, data-free and augmentation-driven methods, and architecture-aware transformations. Practical deployments combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search and must balance transfer of useful teacher information against risks such as propagating teacher errors or overfitting under limited data. The field continues to refine what teacher knowledge to transfer, how to synthesize or augment training data when it is unavailable, and how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures for robust, resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with architecture-aware design, multi-stage training, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and device-constrained deployments. However, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relational signals), teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or synthetic strategies), and operational constraints such as federated heterogeneity and privacy. Practitioners should treat KD as a central tool but evaluate and adapt its signals, data strategy, and integration with other compression techniques to their target deployment scenario.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of model-compression techniques that trains smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior from larger teacher models. Across vision and language tasks, KD methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include alignment of internal representations, attention or relational signals, adversarially-informed objectives, online or multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies. Effective application balances what is transferred, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and robustness or fairness constraints, and it is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models. Methods range from matching teacher outputs (soft logits) to supervising intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and may be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across modalities, but practical success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness to domain shift, and choices about what form of knowledge to distill.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central and practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in both deep learning and natural language processing. KD unifies a range of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and layer-wise objectives, and multi-teacher or data-free variants—and is typically integrated with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The effectiveness of KD depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data; when designed as part of a system-level pipeline KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs but faces open challenges in robustness, domain shift, privacy, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi‑Strategy Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as a toolbox of complementary methods—logit-level supervision, representation matching, layer alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis, and privacy-aware mechanisms—KD enables compact models to approach the performance of larger teachers while meeting real-world constraints on latency, memory, and data access. At the same time, distillation outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices; addressing these limits requires careful method selection and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, first‑line strategy for compressing large deep models for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible transfer channels (soft targets, intermediate features, attention and relational signals) that, when combined with architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, search), yield compact students that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity and alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and careful optimization and evaluation under distribution shift, fairness, and privacy constraints. Practitioners should adopt KD as a toolbox—selecting signals and curricula, aligning representations, and composing KD with other compression methods—while tracking open problems in theoretical guarantees, data-free and private distillation, and robust transfer of rare or domain‑specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and projector-based transforms, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search) and careful teacher–student design, KD routinely yields substantial inference and memory savings while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical application requires attention to teacher quality, data availability, capacity and architecture mismatch, and task-specific objectives (e.g., robustness or privacy); addressing these issues motivates specialized distillation losses, student-aware teacher training, data synthesis, and adversarial or privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. The literature describes a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi‑teacher) and data strategies (original data, augmented or synthetic data, and data‑free variants). KD is frequently combined with architectural or precision changes such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and deployment constraints including privacy and robustness. Best practices treat distillation as a system-level pipeline that integrates pretraining, tailored distillation objectives, and complementary compression techniques to achieve reliable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs in real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible pathway to convert large, high‑performing models into compact students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When matched to student capacity and task constraints, distillation can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while enabling complementary compression (quantization, pruning) and deployment strategies. Realistic application of KD requires attention to what signals are transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, or relational structure), how teacher and student inputs and architectures are aligned, and how limited or synthetic data are used. KD also carries risks—propagation of teacher errors, loss of rare‑token behavior, domain shift sensitivity, and privacy issues—that mandate task‑aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide effective ways to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches span soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and data-free techniques, and multi-teacher or teacher-optimization strategies. Recent work emphasizes task-aware alignment between teacher and student representations, augmentation schemes that improve teacher-student consistency, and training teachers that are explicitly optimized to help downstream students, enabling more reliable deployment in low-resource and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad family of techniques—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—enable deployment of compact models under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in many settings, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and optimization details; careful method selection and combination with complementary compression techniques are therefore central to reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing high-capacity deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD methods span soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate representation and attention matching, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free training. Combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization, distillation enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy for real-world NLP deployments. However, success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, and strategies for handling domain shift, rare-token fidelity, and data- or privacy-constrained settings. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, practical core of compression pipelines and offers concrete recommendations and caveats for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central model-compression approach that trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost, memory, and deployment barriers are reduced while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive behavior. Research has produced a family of distillation objectives (soft-targets, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational losses), training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation, multi-teacher), and system-level integrations (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical studies show well-designed distillation pipelines commonly recover a large fraction of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, but success depends on what knowledge is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical use therefore combines algorithmic choices with architecture-aware compression and data strategies tailored to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, broadly applicable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their predictive power. KD enables large gains in inference speed, reduced memory footprint, and practical deployment under latency, compute, and privacy constraints. However, straightforward distillation can transfer undesirable properties and can underperform when data is limited or teacher–student mismatches are large. To realize KD's full potential practitioners should combine soft-target transfer with representation matching, targeted data augmentation or data-free synthesis, careful teacher design (including ensembles or student-aware teachers), and explicit robustness or privacy-aware objectives. These combined practices produce compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more robust for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-line, Context-aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, how intermediate layers are aligned, and whether data or privacy constraints hold, KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in inference speed and memory. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: optimization difficulties, mismatches in capacity between teacher and student, and limited or private data require tailored objectives, architecture-aware choices, and complementary techniques. This essay argues KD should be a primary strategy in model-compression toolkits while recommending concrete practices to increase reliability across real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide practical pathways to convert large, high-performing models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Empirically, KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations to students that retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness, especially when combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, careful layer or module mapping, and data-management methods. Successful pipelines trade off accuracy, latency, and model size while navigating constraints such as limited or private data and domain shift. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness (including rare-token behavior), aligning heterogeneous architectures, and developing principled data-free or privacy-preserving distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings KD has been shown to recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory footprint. The technique comprises multiple transfer targets (soft outputs/logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and schedules (offline teacher supervision, online co-training, multi-teacher ensembles). Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and must attend to data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, and distributional robustness. Open challenges include data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, reliable transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, and mitigating transfer of biases or teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—logit matching, feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student schemes, and hybrid pipelines combined with pruning or architecture modification—that make it adaptable to diverse deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When applied with attention to the form of transferred knowledge, teacher quality, and data strategies, KD yields compact models suitable for production NLP and cross-modal systems; however, careful design is required to avoid pitfalls such as degraded calibration, transferred biases, or student–teacher mismatch.
