papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and ensemble guidance, online/co-distillation variants, and data- or device-aware adaptations. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search and task-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest loss in accuracy, but persistent challenges remain in handling distribution shift, scarce or private data, transferring rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding unintended transfer of biases. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative application patterns, practical trade-offs, and recommended design choices for applying KD effectively in vision and language systems.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. Its practical success depends strongly on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (or plausible synthetic surrogates), and integration with complementary compression primitives such as pruning and quantization. KD is therefore best treated as a context-dependent component of compression pipelines rather than a single recipe; doing so enables robust, efficient models for a wide range of deep-learning and NLP applications while revealing clear directions for research on heterogeneity, rare-token behavior, and privacy-preserving transfer.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language tasks. KD delivers compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and adaptations for data- or privacy-constrained settings. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, representations, attention maps), how to align teacher and student, and which data strategies and curricula to use. KD should therefore be treated as a first-line, system-level strategy in compression pipelines, but applied with explicit attention to context, complementary techniques, and evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Mechanisms, and Responsible Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practically effective approach for producing compact models that can be deployed under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When treated as a flexible design paradigm rather than a single loss, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), integrates with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization), and adapts to task- and data-specific constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free or synthetic strategies), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behavior. A considered KD pipeline—combining softened logits, representational guidance, task-aware objectives, architecture-aware search, and careful data strategies—yields compact students that meet real-world deployment needs while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical and versatile approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or synthetic data to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with task-aware design, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and appropriate input-side strategies, distillation supports robust deployment across NLP and other modalities. Nevertheless, careful design is required to manage teacher–student mismatch, preserve low-frequency or domain-specific signals, and operate when original training data is limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Current Understandings of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used model compression paradigm in which a smaller student model is trained to capture the behavior of a larger teacher model. It has been applied across domains (vision, NLP, recommender systems, medical imaging) to reduce model size and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Work in the field explores what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, feature relations), how to improve transfer (adversarial samples, contrastive objectives, structural transformations), and how to address practical constraints (absence of original data, domain shift, privacy, fairness and robustness). Empirical results show KD often yields substantial memory and runtime benefits with modest accuracy loss and can be combined with pruning, quantization and architecture search. Yet KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, imperfect teacher signals, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity can limit how closely a student matches a teacher; research continues into theoretical explanations and robust, data-efficient methods.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A spectrum of distillation targets — softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational or contrastive information — and training regimes — offline, online, multi-teacher, or data‑free — enable practitioners to trade model size, latency, and memory for modest predictive degradation. Best practice combines appropriate distillation signals with architecture-aware design, data strategies (including synthetic or filtered data), and complementary compressions (pruning, quantization, low‑precision numerics) so that distilled students meet deployment constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. Remaining gaps include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and long‑tail behaviors in sequence tasks, and explicitly designing distillation strategies for robustness, fairness, and heterogeneous-device constraints.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Rationale, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, first‑line approach for compressing large deep models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible supervision signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses), interoperates with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and has demonstrable empirical success across tasks and modalities. Its practical adoption requires explicit co‑design of teacher and student, careful choice of transferred knowledge, data strategies for scarce or private data, and active mitigation of failure modes (distribution shift, rare-token degradation, and teacher bias).

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring useful predictive and representational knowledge from teacher models to students. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-teacher weighting, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization) and guided by student-aware design and fairness/robustness constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of a teacher's accuracy. Practical deployment of KD requires attention to data availability, teacher quality, and domain-specific constraints to avoid propagating undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. KD techniques — from logits matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, adversarial and data-free variants — enable large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. However, realizing these gains in practice requires task- and student-aware design choices, attention to data and privacy constraints, and explicit strategies to mitigate transferred fragilities. KD is therefore an essential tool in the compression toolbox, but not a universal remedy: careful method selection and evaluation under deployment constraints determine success.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, distillation variants — from logits matching to internal representation transfer, data-free synthesis, online peer-teaching, and AutoML-guided student search — enable deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with task-aware design, multi-teacher curricula, and safeguards for fairness and privacy, KD yields compact models that meet real-world production requirements while preserving most of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD has matured into a flexible toolkit that includes logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware variants. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when the distillation protocol is chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Open challenges remain in data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, preserving rare-token and long-tail behaviors, avoiding propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors (biases or brittleness), and guaranteeing robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Representation-aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, attention- or layer-aware mappings, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-conscious strategies—KD yields compact models that better preserve teacher behavior while meeting deployment constraints. However, realizing those benefits requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, and data constraints; KD is powerful but not a universal remedy.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad, practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, generative, and multimodal domains. Research shows KD can preserve—and in some settings improve—task performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency when combined with complementary strategies. Practical success depends on what is transferred (outputs, internal features, attention), how teacher and student are aligned architecturally and procedurally, and on data and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that the students retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when original data are unavailable, and deploying progressive or ensemble-based strategies. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search) and training-time strategies (curricula, online distillation, or federated protocols) to balance efficiency and accuracy. Despite strong empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and designing principled objectives and curricula that preserve robustness and task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and versatile starting point for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students, but it must be treated as a context‑aware toolkit rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all loss. When co‑designed with student architectures, complemented by representation matching, and adapted to data availability and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Responsible application requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and evaluation under distribution shift, privacy, and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted strategy to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, KD variants have demonstrated the ability to recover much of a teacher model’s performance while substantially reducing inference latency and memory. Practical deployments treat KD as a flexible, system-level primitive—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how to expose students to training data (real, synthesized, or online), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical successes coexist with practical limits: teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and risks of transferring undesirable behaviors or losing robustness remain active research and engineering concerns.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains compact student models to mimic larger teachers so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, practitioners match teacher output distributions, align intermediate representations, synthesize or filter data for student training, and combine distillation with structural compression (pruning, architecture search) to reach deployment targets. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher accuracy and sometimes improve generalization, but outcomes depend on the distillation signal, data provenance, student capacity, and training protocol. Practical deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to present supervision, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques that transfers information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or feature distributions, and can be combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) or data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and provenance of data, and robustness to distributional shifts. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as one element of a broader compression toolkit and apply task- and deployment-aware design choices to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical mechanism for turning large, expensive models into smaller, deployable ones while often preserving much of their predictive quality. KD serves multiple roles beyond pure compression — it regularizes learning, enables domain adaptation, supports heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments, and can be adapted at the logit, feature, or data level. However, its success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, data properties (including low-frequency phenomena), and deployment constraints; KD is therefore a powerful but not universally sufficient tool. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a design paradigm with principled choices (what to transfer, how to adapt teachers, how to combine data and synthetic targets, and how to handle heterogeneity) rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe, and it outlines practical recommendations for applying KD across vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques has been developed—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher or online co-training schedules, and synthesizing or augmenting data for training students. KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, progressive module replacement) and must address open challenges including heterogeneous or federated settings, data scarcity or privacy constraints, robustness under distribution shift, and preservation of low-frequency or domain-specific signals.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks KD variants—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention patterns, multi-teacher and progressive schemes, and self-distillation—have enabled compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success typically requires co-design of the distillation signal, student architecture, data and augmentation choices, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization or pruning). Persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, handling limited or private data, preserving rare-token and robustness properties, and automating trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and adversarially or synthetically generated inputs. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data strategies, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful matching of what is transferred to student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, representative algorithmic families, empirical patterns, and actionable recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. KD operates through multiple channels (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or contrastive signals) and can be combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across NLP, vision, graphs, and sequence generation shows KD often produces compact, deployable models that approach teacher accuracy, but success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability and quality, optimization recipe, and domain-specific constraints. Current research emphasizes designing student-friendly supervision, handling data scarcity or privacy, and extending distillation to heterogeneous or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring useful predictive behavior or internal structure from one or more teachers. A rich set of KD approaches exists — from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate representation imitation, attention and feature alignment, adversarial and projector-based techniques, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or federated variants — and these have been applied across NLP, vision, graph-structured data, multimodal models, and generative models. Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher/student compatibility, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Important practical concerns include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases, enabling privacy-preserving or data-free compression, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search).

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that the students retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when original data are unavailable, and deploying progressive or ensemble-based strategies. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search) and training-time strategies (curricula, online distillation, or federated protocols) to balance efficiency and accuracy. Despite strong empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and designing principled objectives and curricula that preserve robustness and task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention or relational alignment, multi-teacher and online strategies, and task- or data-aware adaptations. Practical compression typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, pretraining, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Success depends on careful matching of distilled signals to the student architecture and deployment constraints; important open problems include handling teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift and heterogeneity, preserving rare or low-frequency information, and maintaining robustness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central Tool for Practical Model Compression, with Limits and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When combined with complementary strategies—such as intermediate-feature alignment, architecture-aware design, data-aware selection, and data-free synthesis—distillation enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. However, KD is not universally sufficient: careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch is required to avoid propagating errors or losing robustness.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multi-Strategy, Practical Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive power while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Best results arise when distillation is combined with complementary techniques — representation matching, ensembling, architecture-aware compression, pretraining of compact students, and data-aware strategies — and when practitioners account for deployment-specific mismatches (domain shift, heterogeneous inputs, or limited access to data). Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rare or low-frequency information, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and designing data-free or privacy-preserving distillation that reliably generalizes under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Principled Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical technique for compressing large neural models into deployable, efficient students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, multi-task, and low-precision settings, distillation can recover large-model accuracy in smaller footprints when combined with careful design choices that address capacity mismatch, task relevance, and the nature of the transferred knowledge. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on distillation schedule, selection of what to transfer (logits, features, or task-aware subsets), and occasionally on teacher improvement or specialization. Understanding these interactions is key to robust compression for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as a core, first‑line strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students when the method is applied as part of a system‑level pipeline. KD reliably reduces inference cost and model size while retaining much of a teacher’s performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, provided practitioners attend to what form of knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with structural compression and data strategies. KD’s strengths are its methodological flexibility (soft targets, feature and attention matching, multi‑teacher schedules, and data synthesis) and its ability to compose with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its principal limits arise from teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and risks of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors; these require explicit remedies (capacity-aware student design, representation projection, multi‑teacher or synthetic data, and robustness evaluation). When deployed as an engineering pipeline rather than a single loss term, KD yields compact models that meet practical latency, memory, and deployment constraints while exposing clear research challenges around robustness, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks KD uses multiple transfer channels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and training regimes (offline teacher supervision, online co-training, multi-teacher ensembles) to recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory. Practical deployments typically combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and must manage data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, and robustness to domain shift and rare behaviors. Remaining challenges concern data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, principled choices of which teacher signals to transfer for a given student and task, and avoiding transfer of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical backbone of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible toolkit to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers to compact students, enabling large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy — its success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data methods), and complementary compression steps; production-grade deployment therefore requires disciplined evaluation of robustness, fairness, and task-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically validated strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through a range of mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, teacher ensembles, and data‑side interventions) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and deployment constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, practitioners must treat it as a context‑sensitive tool and follow best practices to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or encountering failure modes under limited data, heterogeneity, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, distillation methods—ranging from matching teacher soft targets to aligning intermediate features or using data-free synthesis—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical deployments combine distillation with architecture-aware choices (pruning, replacement, or search), multi-teacher or online schemes, and task-aware data strategies. Success depends on teacher quality, choice of transfer targets, data availability, and handling of mismatches; when carefully designed, distillation yields compact, robust models suitable for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal information from teacher models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and are commonly combined with complementary engineering strategies (architecture design, pretraining of compact models, quantization, and data augmentation). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and augmentation, and the relative strength and role of the teacher; these choices shape practical tradeoffs in robustness, fairness, and cross-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their predictive power. When combined with complementary strategies—task-aware objectives, intermediate representation matching, online or distributed schemes, and teacher-student co-design—KD supports deployment on resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive environments. Nonetheless, its effectiveness depends strongly on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including few-shot or data-free regimes), and the choice of distilled signals; recognizing these dependencies leads to principled best practices that balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, deployable models. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, KD has been used to reduce inference cost while retaining most of the teacher model's performance. Research has advanced along several complementary axes: (1) methods that shape what is transferred (logits, hidden representations, attention or task-specific signals), (2) how the transfer is performed (layer-wise, multi-teacher, adversarial or student-aware training), (3) strategies to cope with limited or no access to original training data, and (4) techniques that preserve privacy and improve training efficiency. These lines of work show that careful alignment of objectives, attention to capacity gaps between teacher and student, and tailoring distillation to task and data regimes are critical for effective compression. Remaining challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, principled selection of what to distill for a target task, and maintaining robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques enable deployment of large neural models by transferring knowledge from larger or multi-modal teachers to smaller or specialized students. Work in this area spans methods for structural student design, feature- and logit-level supervision, data-free or few-shot settings, low-precision inference, multi-teacher and domain-adaptive strategies, and automated discovery of compact architectures. Empirical results across vision, speech, language, graph, and generative models show that distillation often achieves substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while preserving much of the teacher performance; however, success depends on data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and training protocols. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, efficient training when teacher cost is high, and principled methods for combining multiple or heterogeneous teachers.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single loss, KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free), and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). I argue KD should serve as the first-line strategy for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes and pair KD with targeted validation for robustness and distributional concerns.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Motivations, and Open Questions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques that transfer information from larger or more complex models (teachers) to smaller or more efficient models (students). These practices are used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large models to constrained or specialized settings (privacy-preserving deployment, edge devices, or faster generation). Across applications—classification, sequence modeling, graph learning, speech, and machine translation—research has explored what to transfer (logits, features, representations), how to transfer it (soft labels, feature projectors, adversarial objectives, data augmentation), and when transfer can fail or require modification (noisy labels, distributional shifts, imperfect teachers). Empirical and theoretical work shows benefits but also identifies trade-offs (regularization vs. fidelity, robustness transfer limits, and data requirements), motivating hybrid approaches that combine pre-training, careful sample selection, and augmentation.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities, but its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, and robustness or fairness objectives. Treating KD as a central building block—combined with architecture-aware compression, representation matching, data strategies, and task-aware curricula—produces the most reliable trade-offs for real deployments. Emerging theoretical analyses and diverse application studies show both why KD works and where it fails, motivating principled combinations of KD with complementary techniques in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, insights, and practical trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in latency-, memory-, and compute-constrained settings. Work across speech, NLP, vision, and graph domains demonstrates a spectrum of approaches: matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing training data for better student generalization, and compressing ensembles into single models. Empirical results show substantial speed and size gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully matched to task and architecture. Important themes include (1) the role of dark/soft labels vs. intermediate feature signals, (2) architectural or task-aware compression (including search), (3) techniques that increase the student’s exposure to informative training points (e.g., mixup or adversarial examples), and (4) distillation strategies tailored for ensembles or heterogeneous teacher–student pairs. Open challenges remain in principled sample selection, robust transfer of inductive biases, and automated trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are essential tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. A wide family of methods — from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature transfer, projector-based alignment, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture search — let practitioners trade compute and memory for modest accuracy loss. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on optimization, data alignment, and the choice of distilled signals; it can replicate undesirable teacher behaviors and fails when teacher–student mismatch or data constraints are not addressed. Practical deployment therefore requires selecting KD variants that match application constraints and combining distillation with complementary compression and robustness techniques.
