papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Work across vision and language shows a set of recurring strategies: transfer using softened outputs (soft targets), imitation of intermediate/internal representations, layer mapping between teacher and student, task-adaptive architecture search, self-distillation, and data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable. Empirical results indicate that properly designed distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while offering large gains in inference speed and memory; however, success depends on which knowledge is transferred (outputs vs. internal features), how layers are aligned, and whether task specificity and data availability are addressed. The field currently balances practical engineering (architecture and search) with algorithmic refinements (losses and training regimes), and open challenges include robust data-free methods, principled many-to-many layer matching, and teacher designs that are optimized to be “student-friendly.”

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a toolbox rather than a single loss term, KD delivers meaningful efficiency gains across modalities when the distillation targets, student design, and data strategy are chosen for the deployment constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis methods, and robustness to distribution shift. Practical success therefore requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, carefully selecting what to transfer, and evaluating students under realistic deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has been adapted beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature supervision, layer- or module-level mapping, selective sample transfer, data-free synthesis, and combinations with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments reveal important dependencies on teacher quality, student architecture, data availability, and training protocols; when these are handled deliberately, distilled models can achieve strong trade-offs in accuracy, latency, and resource use. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, preserving low-frequency or rare outputs, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures in privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students retain much of the teachers’ functionality while being cheaper to run. KD operates through multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation). In practice KD is most effective when treated as a system-level pipeline that reconciles teacher–student mismatches, leverages appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized), and combines with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). The method reliably improves deployment trade-offs in many settings, but its success is context-dependent: it is sensitive to teacher quality and alignment, data availability and provenance, student capacity, and distributional or privacy constraints. Open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Barker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line but Contextual Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD provides multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and training regimes (offline teacher-to-student, online/self-distillation, ensemble-to-single), and it can be combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. However, KD’s success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, the choice of what knowledge to transfer, data availability or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness and privacy. Treated as a core element of a compression pipeline rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all remedy, KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for many real-world applications while leaving important open problems in data-free distillation, rare-behavior preservation, and distributional robustness.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention/relational signals, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthesized-data variants—that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior. KD therefore functions best as a central component within a broader compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and teacher-free/self-distillation variants. KD is most effective when treated as a system-level design choice—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost with modest performance loss, its success depends on data availability, optimization dynamics, teacher quality, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness; open challenges remain around domain shift, preserving rare-token behaviors in language models, privacy-aware distillation, and principled data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expressive models to smaller, efficient models to enable practical deployment without excessive loss in performance. These methods include matching teacher soft outputs, feature-level alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and architecture-aware strategies for heterogeneous settings. Across domains—vision, speech, NLP, and recommender systems—distillation is used both to compress models for latency and memory constraints and to inject complementary knowledge (e.g., cross-task or cross-modal signals). Empirical work shows that careful design choices (e.g., mixing hard/soft targets, projector modules, or student-aware teacher training) and task-specific adaptations address common pitfalls such as information loss on rare tokens or domain shifts. Open directions include stronger theoretical understanding, robustness under imperfect teachers, and principled integration with quantization, federated settings, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Principled Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive power. KD is most effective when it goes beyond naïve soft-label copying: matching internal representations, aligning inputs and tokenization, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and adapting teacher updates or curricula all materially affect transfer quality. KD should be used as part of a broader compression pipeline (architecture design, quantization, pruning, or data strategies) and with explicit checks for rare-token behavior, fairness, and robustness. When applied with these considerations, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for production constraints in vision, language, and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones that remain useful in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD supports a wide range of operational needs: output- and feature-level transfer, data- and teacher-aware strategies, privacy-preserving distributed training, and task-adaptive compression. Realizing KD’s benefits in production requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to combine distillation with complementary methods such as architecture search, pruning, task-aware layer selection, and synthetic-data techniques.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a unifying strategy that addresses model size, inference latency, domain shifts, multimodal transfer, privacy, and training efficiency. By transferring supervisory signals, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger or more capable systems, KD enables compact student models to retain much of the performance of cumbersome teachers while meeting practical deployment constraints. When combined with task-aware architecture search, layer-mapping techniques, and online or domain-aware protocols, distillation offers a principled path to build small, fast, and adaptable models across diverse settings.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students that retain much of the teacher's performance. Across NLP, vision, and generative models, KD takes many forms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free synthesis) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving accuracy under many conditions, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and optimization protocols. Practical deployment requires careful design choices and remains an active area for research on robustness, rare-token preservation, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact models by transferring richer supervision from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD encompasses multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational maps), supports various training regimes (offline teacher-to-student, online/co‑distillation, multi‑teacher ensembles), and composes with structural compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Its practical success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthetic-data strategies, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness. Treating KD as a design pipeline—selecting appropriate signals, aligning representations, adapting data strategies, and combining with complementary compression—yields students that meet real‑world deployment constraints while reducing common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including domain adaptation and black-box/data-free workflows). In practice KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures, combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and tailored to data availability and deployment constraints. Despite wide empirical success across vision and NLP, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, distilling rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable compression when training data are limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: State of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces inference cost by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models. The field has evolved from simple soft‑label matching to a rich set of techniques that transfer logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and that integrate with architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data strategies. Practical deployments rely on matching the form of distilled knowledge to student capacity and task constraints, using pre‑training or task‑aware adaptation when possible, and addressing optimization and data limitations. Remaining challenges include data‑free distillation, robustness and fairness under compression, domain shift, and principled choices for heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression: Powerful, Practical, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and optimization interactions. I argue that KD should serve as the default first-line method in compression toolkits, but practitioners must treat it as a design paradigm that is complemented by targeted validation and additional compression methods where needed.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical and versatile approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or synthetic data to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with task-aware design, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and appropriate input-side strategies, distillation supports robust deployment across NLP and other modalities. Nevertheless, careful design is required to manage teacher–student mismatch, preserve low-frequency or domain-specific signals, and operate when original training data is limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Foundation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD spans logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, progressive architecture replacement, adversarial and data-free variants, and combinations with structural compression and pruning. When applied with attention to the distilled signal, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and optimization protocol, KD reliably reduces memory, latency, and compute costs across vision, language, generative, and graph domains. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on careful method selection, complementary compression steps, and mitigation of teacher–student mismatch and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving predictive performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, contrastive and relational signals, online or teacher-free co-training, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data availability; remaining challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and reliable distillation when original data are limited or private.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single loss term, KD reliably improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities and tasks. Its success depends on deliberate choices about what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. Important open problems remain around distribution shift, low-frequency behaviors, privacy- and data-constrained settings, and principled data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD succeeds when its objectives, representation targets, and training regimes are chosen to match deployment constraints and student capacity; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, data-free synthesis, and online protocols) extends its reach. However, KD also transfers risks (bias, privacy leakage, fragility) and faces limits when teacher signals are mismatched or training data are scarce, motivating task-aware design, robust distillation objectives, and emergent meta- and data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, transferring intermediate representations or attentions, leveraging ensembles or self-teaching, and operating in constrained settings via data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Across vision, generative models, and natural language tasks, distillation is used both as a standalone compression technique and as a complement to pruning and quantization. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability, and how to mitigate optimization and distributional mismatches. While KD often produces compact models that approach teacher performance, practical deployment requires careful design to avoid failure modes arising from heterogeneous data, limited student capacity, or misaligned training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective strategy for compressing large models into efficient students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains. Beyond simply matching teacher logits, modern KD benefits from teaching intermediate representations, mimicking teacher features, self-distillation, and careful handling of multiple or stronger teachers. KD also composes well with structured pruning and other compression techniques to meet hardware constraints. This article synthesizes empirical lessons and recommended practices for applying KD reliably in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework that enables transferring predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, deployable ones. KD supports diverse practical constraints — absent training data, limited downstream-task data, domain shifts, multi-task settings, and architectural mismatches — and couples naturally with automated model search and targeted feature imitation. By viewing KD as a family of techniques (logit transfer, feature mimicking, adversarial-sample guidance, synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-ensemble strategies) practitioners can compress models while retaining or even improving task-relevant inductive structure and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become primary tools to shrink large deep models for deployment while retaining much of their predictive power. Across vision, speech and natural language processing, researchers have developed a range of approaches that operate at the level of logits (soft labels), intermediate representations, modules/layers, or training curricula, and have combined KD with complementary strategies such as architecture search, quantization, and generative replay. Empirical work shows that distilled students can often approach teacher performance while achieving large reductions in size and latency, but the effectiveness of different KD strategies depends strongly on task, data distribution, teacher strength, and practical constraints such as availability of original training data. Important challenges remain in transferring robustness, handling heterogeneous or private data, preserving rare-token behavior, and balancing bias–variance tradeoffs introduced by soft supervision.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving or even improving generalization. The field combines a variety of approaches — from logit-level transfer to feature- and attention-level imitation, from data-free synthesis to multi-teacher ensembles and task-adaptive architecture search — and is applied across domains including NLP, vision, speech and healthcare. Contemporary work integrates distillation with pruning, neural architecture search, federated and privacy-preserving training, and meta-learning for better teacher-student alignment. Empirical results show substantial compression and speedups with modest accuracy loss when distillation is combined with architecture-aware optimization and data- or task-aware strategies. Ongoing challenges include handling imperfect teachers, distribution shift of synthetic data, privacy constraints, and transferring inductive biases across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach that should be treated as the first-line, system-level strategy for compressing large models into deployable students. When KD is applied as a design primitive — selecting which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods and data strategies — it yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, reliable deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for shrinking high-capacity models into smaller, deployable models while retaining much of their performance. When applied thoughtfully — with attention to what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations), how to align teachers and students (layer mapping, task-aware filters), and how to handle data constraints (data-free synthesis, federated heterogeneity, privacy) — KD enables latency- and memory-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and generative settings. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher–student capacity matching, the choice of distilled signals, and addressing data heterogeneity or absence. The evidence suggests KD should be treated as a flexible toolkit combined with complementary strategies (architecture search, quantization, data augmentation) to meet real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logits-matching into a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention matching, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, data- and teacher-free variants, and system-level integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs when teacher–student capacity, distillation targets, and data strategies are chosen thoughtfully, but its effectiveness is context-dependent: data availability, distributional shift, architecture compatibility, and task-specific behaviors can limit transfer and require tailored evaluation and mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad set of practical recipes—including logit (soft-target) supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and joint use with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—enable deployment of compact models across vision, language, and graph tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while reducing compute and memory, but effectiveness depends on the choice of transfer target, availability or synthesis of suitable data, student architecture, and training dynamics. Key open issues remain around principled explanations for when distillation helps, reliably transferring robustness and fairness properties, privacy-aware distillation, and automating student design for specific resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Practical Role and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, faster models suitable for production and edge deployment. Different KD variants—data-free, multi-teacher, online, feature-level, adversarial, and task-specific strategies—address practical constraints like lack of original data, communication or privacy limits, and the need to preserve representational quality. However, KD is not a panacea: its benefits depend on teacher-student capacity, dataset complexity, optimization choices, and the design of distillation signals. A pragmatic approach selects KD variants that match the application constraints and explicitly addresses optimization and data-complexity issues to maximize student performance while preserving efficiency and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher to student. A diverse set of approaches extend the basic soft-label paradigm to include internal representation matching, layer-wise and attention-guided alignment, task-aware selection of distilled features, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, augmentation-driven consistency, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, adversarial learning objectives, and architecture search tailored to downstream tasks. These techniques improve inference efficiency while aiming to preserve accuracy, generalization, and task-specific behavior; they also enable distillation in settings with limited or no access to original training data and in generation tasks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, selecting which teacher knowledge to preserve for a given student capacity and task, and designing robust distilled models that generalize across domains and data shifts.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to reduce the runtime, memory, and deployment costs of large deep models while retaining their predictive performance or improving other desiderata (e.g., interpretability, fairness). Across vision and language domains, methods range from classical teacher-to-student soft-target distillation to transferring intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, selective sample-driven distillation, and teacher-adaptive or teacher-free schemes. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation targets, alignment of intermediate representations, and input-side practices (such as tailored data augmentation) can materially affect student performance. Remaining challenges include representation mismatches between teacher and student, identifying which training samples are beneficial for transfer, and adapting distillation to domain- or resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, first‑line strategy for compressing large deep models for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible transfer channels (soft targets, intermediate features, attention and relational signals) that, when combined with architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, search), yield compact students that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity and alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and careful optimization and evaluation under distribution shift, fairness, and privacy constraints. Practitioners should adopt KD as a toolbox—selecting signals and curricula, aligning representations, and composing KD with other compression methods—while tracking open problems in theoretical guarantees, data-free and private distillation, and robust transfer of rare or domain‑specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD supports a broad set of objectives—matching logits, aligning internal representations, using online or multi-teacher schemes, and operating with or without original training data—so it serves as the backbone of many modern compression pipelines. However, its success is context-dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability, and deployment constraints determine outcomes, and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and principled training workflows.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints; it is applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and is routinely combined with complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s benefits depend strongly on choices about what is distilled (logits, features, attention, relational structure), teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free settings), and deployment constraints; addressing domain shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and avoiding undesirable property transfer remain important open challenges. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central component of modern compression pipelines while recognizing its context-dependent limits and recommending pragmatic combinations with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, deployable models. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, KD has been used to reduce inference cost while retaining most of the teacher model's performance. Research has advanced along several complementary axes: (1) methods that shape what is transferred (logits, hidden representations, attention or task-specific signals), (2) how the transfer is performed (layer-wise, multi-teacher, adversarial or student-aware training), (3) strategies to cope with limited or no access to original training data, and (4) techniques that preserve privacy and improve training efficiency. These lines of work show that careful alignment of objectives, attention to capacity gaps between teacher and student, and tailoring distillation to task and data regimes are critical for effective compression. Remaining challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, principled selection of what to distill for a target task, and maintaining robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Backbone with Bounded Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical strategy for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and, when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression techniques, yields efficient models suitable for latency- and memory-constrained deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design, and practitioners must address robustness, fairness, and task-specific constraints to realize reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and other modalities. A broad family of techniques transfers different forms of teacher information — from softened logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data-free synthesis and adversarially guided generation). Empirical evidence shows that, when carefully designed to match teacher–student capacity and data conditions, KD can retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, mitigating bias transfer, and characterizing when particular distillation objectives succeed in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: The Pragmatic Power and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured into a practical toolkit for shrinking models, transferring behavior across architectures and modalities, and enabling deployment under compute, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond straightforward teacher-to-student compression, distillation techniques combine with data augmentation, synthetic-data generation, and regularization to address limited data, cross-domain gaps, and interpretability needs. However, outcomes depend on choices about teacher quality, training data availability, and objective design; careful method selection is required to realize reliable, production-ready gains.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Central, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD methods span soft‑label/ logits transfer, intermediate‑feature and attention matching, adversarial and data‑free approaches, and teacher‑student co‑training or meta‑learned teachers. When thoughtfully designed — selecting appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student capacities, and addressing data availability and robustness requirements — KD enables practical deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. However, KD is not universally successful: its effectiveness depends on architecture compatibility, quality and coverage of data (or of synthetic surrogates), and task‑specific choices, so practitioners must evaluate distillation under realistic conditions and adopt best practices tailored to their constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD operates at multiple levels (softened output distributions, intermediate features and attention maps, relational/contrastive objectives, and module-level behavior), and is commonly combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (data-free synthesis, public transfer sets, augmentation). Empirical work shows well-designed KD pipelines often produce compact models that approach teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and careful choice of distillation signals. Open problems include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, ensuring robustness under distribution shift, and developing principled teacher design and data-limited protocols.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed not as a single trick but as a central, system-level toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student co-design, suitable data strategies (including synthesis or data-free protocols), and deployment-aware training schedules, KD yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability; it also raises risks around transferring biases, losing rare-token behaviors, and underperforming under distribution shift. Treating KD as a first-line, flexible approach within a broader compression pipeline — rather than a one-size-fits-all cure — produces the most reliable outcomes for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression: Effectiveness, Limits, and Practical Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When treated as a system—choosing which signals to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning teacher and student architectures, managing data and sample selection, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks. Its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and attention to robustness and rare-token behavior; hence KD is best used as the central element of a broader compression pipeline rather than as a standalone fix.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Over the past decade KD methods have diversified beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher pipelines, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive compression. Empirical work across NLP, speech, vision-language, and other domains shows KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while drastically reducing model size and latency. Theoretical and empirical analyses have clarified why KD works in many settings (regularization via soft targets, ensemble-induced dark knowledge, and representation enrichment), but open problems remain in data privacy, distribution shift, automated student design, and guarantees for out-of-distribution robustness.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of distillation objectives—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention- and channel-guided losses, relational/contrastive signals, and self- or multi-teacher regimes—can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity, access to (or synthesis of) suitable training data, and mitigation of optimization, fairness, and robustness risks. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative methods, practical recommendations, and open challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework that enables transferring predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, deployable ones. KD supports diverse practical constraints — absent training data, limited downstream-task data, domain shifts, multi-task settings, and architectural mismatches — and couples naturally with automated model search and targeted feature imitation. By viewing KD as a family of techniques (logit transfer, feature mimicking, adversarial-sample guidance, synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-ensemble strategies) practitioners can compress models while retaining or even improving task-relevant inductive structure and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a unifying strategy that addresses model size, inference latency, domain shifts, multimodal transfer, privacy, and training efficiency. By transferring supervisory signals, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger or more capable systems, KD enables compact student models to retain much of the performance of cumbersome teachers while meeting practical deployment constraints. When combined with task-aware architecture search, layer-mapping techniques, and online or domain-aware protocols, distillation offers a principled path to build small, fast, and adaptable models across diverse settings.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques constitute a flexible toolkit for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. Across speech, vision, and natural language tasks, practitioners transfer predictive behavior and selected internal structure from teachers to students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while preserving task performance. The literature shows a spectrum of methods (soft-targets, representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free approaches), trade-offs that depend on student capacity and data access, and practical strategies that pair distillation with pretraining, architecture design, and data interventions. Important limitations remain around domain shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, theoretical characterization of what transfers, and privacy-aware or data-free distillation regimes.
