papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad, practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, generative, and multimodal domains. Research shows KD can preserve—and in some settings improve—task performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency when combined with complementary strategies. Practical success depends on what is transferred (outputs, internal features, attention), how teacher and student are aligned architecturally and procedurally, and on data and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Integrated Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, flexible means to produce compact models for deployment in compute-, memory-, or privacy-constrained settings. When chosen and applied with attention to what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits depend on principled design and evaluation, and it should be integrated into broader compression pipelines rather than used in isolation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and other modalities. A broad family of techniques transfers different forms of teacher information — from softened logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data-free synthesis and adversarially guided generation). Empirical evidence shows that, when carefully designed to match teacher–student capacity and data conditions, KD can retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, mitigating bias transfer, and characterizing when particular distillation objectives succeed in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment. When combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, careful attention to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and domain shift is required to preserve robustness and rare or domain-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language processing. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students using a variety of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and configurations (single- or multi-teacher, online/offline, data-driven or data-free). When combined with complementary compression techniques and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models with substantially reduced inference cost while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, the type and availability of data used for transfer, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness, and so KD is best applied as one element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices for what and how to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), and when combined with complementary compression strategies (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Practical compression pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core tool whose design must be tailored to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have diversified from the original logits-based teacher→student paradigm into a broad set of methods that operate on features, modules, data, and training procedures. Contemporary work shows multiple complementary mechanisms for transferring knowledge—soft targets, feature- and attention-level mimicry, adversarial alignment, module replacement, and data- or communication-constrained distillation—each suited to different deployment constraints (privacy, compute, bandwidth) and model families (transformers, CNNs, GANs, GNNs). Advances emphasize (1) understanding why KD helps (stability, richer concept learning), (2) designing where to transfer knowledge (penultimate features, attention maps, projectors), and (3) tailoring the distillation process to practical settings (online multi-model training, federated environments, data-free scenarios, and teacher models optimized for students). Empirical results across vision, speech, language, generation, and retrieval indicate KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance when the distillation objective, the representation level, and the training dynamics are appropriately matched to the target constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level, Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Its value arises from flexible choices about what and how to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to expose students to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online signals), and how to combine distillation with architecture and numerical compression. However, distillation is not automatic: teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or privacy constraints, and deployment targets (latency, memory, robustness, fairness) materially affect outcomes. Viewing distillation as a system-level primitive — one part of a broader compression and deployment pipeline — yields better, more reliable trade-offs between efficiency and retained capability.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities, but its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, and robustness or fairness objectives. Treating KD as a central building block—combined with architecture-aware compression, representation matching, data strategies, and task-aware curricula—produces the most reliable trade-offs for real deployments. Emerging theoretical analyses and diverse application studies show both why KD works and where it fails, motivating principled combinations of KD with complementary techniques in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring useful information from large teacher models to smaller students. Methods span soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, and data-free or zero‑shot synthesis to handle unavailable or private training data. KD is typically combined with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and training practices (curricula, augmentation) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Despite strong empirical success across vision, speech, and NLP, important limitations remain: principled theory of when distillation helps, reliable transfer of robustness and fairness, handling distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena, and automated student design for specific resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students so the students retain most of the teachers' performance while meeting resource constraints. The literature frames KD as a multifaceted toolbox that includes soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, task-adaptive schedules, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, but success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity and architecture alignment, the provenance and availability of data, and training/optimization dynamics. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require careful choices of distillation signals, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness. Key open problems include reliable data-free distillation, preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior, principled teacher design, and theoretical characterization of when specific knowledge sources help.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques has been developed—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher or online co-training schedules, and synthesizing or augmenting data for training students. KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, progressive module replacement) and must address open challenges including heterogeneous or federated settings, data scarcity or privacy constraints, robustness under distribution shift, and preservation of low-frequency or domain-specific signals.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when its objectives, training dynamics, and data strategies are co‑designed with student architectures and deployment constraints. However, distillation is context‑dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, optimization dynamics, and explicit handling of rare or safety‑critical behaviors. Consequently, KD should be used as a default first‑line tool within integrated compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design) and applied with targeted diagnostics and mitigation steps for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic training trick into a unifying framework for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and language tasks. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus from larger teachers to smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while largely preserving accuracy. Beyond plain size reduction, KD adapts to constraints that arise in real deployments — limited data or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogeneous architectures, and modality gaps — through techniques such as feature-level alignment, selective sampling, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, and data-free synthesis. As a practical bridge between research-scale architectures and deployable systems, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and serves both as an efficiency accelerator and as a lever for robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a toolbox rather than a single loss term, KD delivers meaningful efficiency gains across modalities when the distillation targets, student design, and data strategy are chosen for the deployment constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis methods, and robustness to distribution shift. Practical success therefore requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, carefully selecting what to transfer, and evaluating students under realistic deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a pragmatic and flexible approach to compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in size and compute while retaining much of a teacher model's performance, and it adapts well to modalities from vision to speech and to task-specific constraints in NLP. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, mismatches between teacher and student, and the potential for poorer outcomes when distilling inappropriate teacher signals require careful method selection and evaluation. Best practice therefore combines tailored distillation architectures, curriculum or multi-teacher strategies, privacy-aware mechanisms where needed, and awareness of when label-smoothing or teacher-free alternatives are preferable.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP: a multifaceted toolkit that reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when combined with careful design choices. KD succeeds because it can transfer soft predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and relational structure, and because it composes naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, and privacy-preserving proxies). However, KD is not a universal cure — its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, access to appropriate data (or viable data-free alternatives), and explicit handling of robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy constraints. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core, configurable element of compression pipelines and pair it with targeted engineering, diagnostics, and domain-aware choices to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD systems can leverage soft-targets, internal representation matching, teacher ensembles, or teacher-free regularizers to transfer performance characteristics to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving accuracy. However, the success of KD depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; achieving reliable, fair, and robust compression typically requires combining complementary strategies and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, But Not the Whole, of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD scales across modalities and deployment regimes, enabling latency-, memory-, and communication-constrained applications. However, distillation is not a drop-in cure: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and students are co-designed, the availability and provenance of data, and safeguards for fairness, robustness, and privacy. A pragmatic stance treats KD as a system-level primitive that should be combined with complementary techniques (data synthesis, representation matching, multi-teacher curricula, and privacy-aware ensembles) to realize reliable, efficient models in real-world NLP and deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, data-free or few-shot protocols). Practical outcomes depend on teacher quality and specialization, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability; open problems include reliable transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and operating under privacy or data-limited constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and effective strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. KD operates through multiple knowledge channels (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relations, and ensembles) and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data-free synthesis). While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and supports deployment under tight resource or privacy constraints, its success is context-dependent: teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and robustness or calibration requirements determine outcomes. Best practice treats KD as a design pipeline—choose task-appropriate transfer targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, leverage teacher ensembles or task-adaptive searches when helpful, and use data-aware or data-free methods where necessary.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical backbone of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible toolkit to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers to compact students, enabling large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy — its success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data methods), and complementary compression steps; production-grade deployment therefore requires disciplined evaluation of robustness, fairness, and task-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Practitioners apply KD not only as a logits-matching loss but as a system-level design primitive that includes representation matching, multi-teacher fusion, data and curriculum design, and combination with pruning and quantization. Its empirical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational signals), how to map teacher signals to potentially heterogeneous students, and how to handle limited or private data. While KD often yields compact models with near-teacher performance and useful regularization effects, limitations remain: imperfect teacher signals, optimization challenges, robustness and fairness transfer, and domain-shift or data-scarce scenarios. Current best practices emphasize task-aware selection of distilled signals, layer/projector alignment, and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with other compression techniques to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become the primary, practical method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD unifies multiple training strategies—soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis—enabling substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search) and when its objectives and data regimes are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints. Despite its strengths, KD has known weaknesses, including sensitivity to teacher–student mismatch, degradation under data heterogeneity, and risks of transferring undesirable behaviors; addressing these requires careful protocol design, selective transfer of teacher signals, and hybrid pipelines that integrate KD with data-centric and architecture-centric interventions.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful teacher–student co-design, distillation provides a practical first-line strategy for real-world model compression, though important open problems remain around fairness, data availability, heterogeneity, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, methods range from classic teacher-student logits supervision to data-free and online schemes, meta-learned teachers, and representation-level transfers. Empirical work shows KD often yields substantial efficiency gains but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, model capacity, data availability, and optimization choices; important failure modes and practical remediation strategies have been identified.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD should be treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is chosen and tuned to match teacher–student capacity, data availability, deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy), and architectural heterogeneity. When designed with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), projector or alignment modules, and complementary compression techniques, distillation reliably enables compact, efficient models for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications. However, careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and domain shift is required to avoid failure modes and degraded behavior.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques has been developed—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher or online co-training schedules, and synthesizing or augmenting data for training students. KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, progressive module replacement) and must address open challenges including heterogeneous or federated settings, data scarcity or privacy constraints, robustness under distribution shift, and preservation of low-frequency or domain-specific signals.

papers_seen.author: Singh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and a Pragmatic Integration Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded approach for converting large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a multi-signal toolbox rather than a single loss, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while preserving much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal cure: its success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, and targeted remedies for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy. A practical stance treats KD as the central element of a hybrid compression pipeline that deliberately combines representation-aware objectives, architecture-aware choices, and data-aware or privacy-preserving workflows to realize reliable, efficient models for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Effective and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Risks, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large, high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. KD delivers large gains in inference speed and memory while preserving much of the teacher's utility across NLP tasks (including question answering and sentence understanding) and other modalities. However, naive distillation can transfer undesirable properties such as bias, privacy leakage, or fragility to distribution shift and adversarial attacks. A combination of strategies—student-aware teacher design, multi-teacher curricula, selective sample distillation, data augmentation, adversarial and robust distillation, and privacy-aware ensembles—provides a pragmatic path to compress models while controlling fairness, robustness, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. Methods extend beyond simple soft-target (logit) matching to include alignment of intermediate representations, attention maps, relational structure, and architecture-aware adaptations. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data‑free approaches), and training curricula (annealing, multi-teacher or online schedules). Empirical work across vision and language shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and design choices that affect robustness, fairness, and generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware techniques, and deployment-aware protocols, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and device heterogeneity to be met. Best practices include selecting appropriate distilled signals (beyond soft labels), pretraining or warming students, and aligning objectives with deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical success across modalities, open challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, domain shift, privacy-sensitive settings, and the automated design of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. A rich toolbox has emerged—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with structural compression—that makes it possible to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, data availability, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and domain-specific behavior, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatch in heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Targeted Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller students. The field has evolved beyond matching softened output logits to include representation-level guidance, attention and relational targets, data-augmentation and synthesis strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision and language shows that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while reducing compute, memory, and latency; however, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and provenance, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as one component of a compression toolkit, integrating architecture choices, precision reductions, and data strategies to meet production constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed with attention to which signals are transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data constraints are handled, KD often preserves most of a teacher's performance while delivering large gains in inference latency, memory, and deployability. KD is most effective as part of a system-level compression pipeline that pairs representation matching with architecture-aware student design and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). It is not a universal remedy: poor teacher–student compatibility, limited or mismatched data, and concerns about robustness, fairness, and privacy can limit outcomes. Responsible application therefore treats KD as the default first step for compression but requires task-aware objective design, data strategies, and targeted evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that high-performing systems can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; they can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-design choices to meet hardware and application requirements. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can improve student generalization, but outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or federated settings), and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a flexible component in a broader compression strategy and adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and student architectures to the target deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade a diverse family of distillation methods has emerged—logit-level soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, multi-teacher ensembles, and privacy-aware adaptations—applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data availability and domain mismatch; combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture search, quantization) and task-aware pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: The Centrality of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision and language tasks, distillation can act both as a compression mechanism and as a regularizer, and it integrates naturally with complementary strategies such as architecture search, layer-wise alignment, representation matching, data augmentation, pruning, and deployment-aware methods. When applied thoughtfully—matching teacher and student representations, tuning the signal provided by soft labels, and adapting to task or device constraints—distillation enables practical, high-performing compressed models suitable for production and edge settings.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Practical Strengths, Limits, and a Pragmatic Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of methods for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Over a range of modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive objectives), and they can be combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or synthetic-data generation) to meet deployment constraints. KD reliably improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when teacher and student are properly aligned and when the distillation strategy matches data and system constraints; however, it is not a universal solution. Key limitations include sensitivity to teacher–student capacity mismatch, degraded transfer on low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena, and challenges when original training data are unavailable or under distribution shift. A pragmatic KD practice chooses appropriate distilled signals, co-designs student architectures, uses synthetic or adversarially generated data when needed, and evaluates robustness and fairness under realistic deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded toolkit that enables compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when paired with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods. However, its effectiveness is context-dependent: success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy concerns. Treating KD as the backbone of an integrated compression pipeline delivers the best practical outcomes while acknowledging and mitigating its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi-strategy toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision and natural language processing. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) and are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful choice of distilled signals and training schedules; remaining challenges include data-free distillation, heterogeneity between architectures, robustness and fairness under compression, and preservation of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive power. A variety of mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate feature imitation, layer- or module-level mappings, and architecture-aware search—enable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, model size, and privacy. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact architectures, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, and privacy-preserving synthesis) and tailor choices to data availability, task constraints, and target hardware. Despite broad empirical success, open issues remain around transferring robustness and rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and designing distillation pipelines that are robust under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Core, Proven Benefits, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what is transferred (logits, features, attention maps, or relations), how teachers and students are co-designed, and how data and deployment constraints are handled, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, and explicit treatment of robustness and privacy. Practical pipelines therefore combine KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and robustness/privacy objectives to produce compact models suitable for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and inputs, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely reduces model size and latency while preserving much task performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., rare-token behavior), so careful protocol design and evaluation under realistic constraints are essential.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s predictive power. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention and relational signals, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data- or privacy-aware variants. In practice, KD is most effective when co-designed with student architecture, data handling (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, KD’s benefits are context-dependent: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful selection of which signals to transfer; open challenges remain around robustness, long-tail or rare-token behavior, and principled choices for heterogeneous teacher–student pairings.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad family of techniques—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—enable deployment of compact models under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in many settings, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and optimization details; careful method selection and combination with complementary compression techniques are therefore central to reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying deep models under resource constraints. Methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-layer supervision, feature mimicking, projector-based transforms, teacher-student co-training, and data- or domain-aware schemes. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs) and in settings with limited or no access to original training data. Practical advances address transfer across architectures, task-adaptive compression, and efficient architecture search, while open problems remain around distribution shift, heterogeneity of data or detectors, and preserving rare or low-frequency information.
