papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger, often more expensive teacher models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Research over the past decade has developed a spectrum of KD objectives (soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational losses), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online co-training, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules), and deployment-aware integrations (pre-training students, architecture-aware adapters, and combination with pruning or quantization). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while reducing parameter count and latency, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and the choice of what and how to transfer. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, matching heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals, and automating trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compress large deep models and transfer knowledge to smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. Across vision and language applications, KD encompasses teacher-student paradigms that use teacher soft targets, intermediate representations, or auxiliary objectives; extensions include multi-teacher setups, data-free distillation, meta-learned teachers, and device-aware distillation for heterogeneous deployments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in parameters and inference cost; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and how dataset complexity, teacher quality, and student capacity interact to determine outcomes. Practical strategies combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques to meet deployment constraints while retaining generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable smaller or faster models to retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific inductive biases. Work in this area spans supervised soft-target matching, intermediate-layer representation transfer, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, and online/distributed variants that exploit parallelism. Applications include compressing large pretrained language models for downstream NLP tasks, accelerating inference for computer vision and generative models, and producing interpretable or privacy-preserving compact models for healthcare and on-device deployment. Important trade-offs involve what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, activations, relations), access to training data, robustness to domain heterogeneity, and how to balance capacity, efficiency, and generalization in student models.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods that transfers richer supervision from large teacher models to compact students in order to reduce inference cost while retaining predictive performance. KD covers logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, channel- and feature-level transfers, self- and online-distillation, and multi-teacher and data-free variants. Its effectiveness depends on alignment between teacher and student capacity, the choice of what to transfer, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a central component of modern compression pipelines but always applied with task- and context-aware adaptations and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven strategy for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller students suitable for real-world deployment. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher model’s utility. However, KD is not a single recipe: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how teachers and students are aligned, and the availability and provenance of data. Treating KD as a system-level primitive — combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), informed data strategies, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness — yields the best practical tradeoffs while highlighting open challenges in few-shot, privacy-sensitive, and domain-shifted settings.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques reliably reduce large pretrained models to compact, efficient students suitable for deployment while preserving most of the teacher performance. Across NLP and multimodal tasks, practical compression requires strategies that (1) align representations at multiple levels, (2) focus on task-relevant information, and (3) handle limited or no access to original training data. Combining architecture-aware search, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, and improved input-side strategies (including data augmentation or data-free sample generation) yields compact models with strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs suitable for real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. KD methods span soft-target matching, representation-level supervision, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data‑free or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student co‑design, KD yields deployable models that meet latency and memory constraints across vision and language tasks. Yet KD is not a single recipe: its effectiveness depends on the information transferred, teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and domain match, and attention to robustness and fairness. The pragmatic view treats KD as a flexible toolkit that must be adapted to context and combined with other interventions for reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a family of methods that include feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and projection, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful design choices about which signals to transfer. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or undesirable behaviors. This synthesis summarizes common methods, mechanisms, practical patterns, and outstanding limitations to guide researchers and practitioners applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original model's utility. Empirical results across vision, language, recommendation, and generation tasks show that carefully designed distillation—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate feature and relational transfer, online co-training, and progressive module replacement—enables large reductions in latency and memory with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and augmentation, and targeted mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, and privacy leakage. Treating KD as a system-level primitive and combining it with complementary compression and data strategies yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted strategy for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD has been adapted into a family of techniques that vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), how transfer is scheduled (offline, online, multi-teacher), and how data constraints are handled (real-data, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). In practice, KD is most effective when treated as a system-level design primitive and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, student-aware architecture design) and data strategies, but its success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse forms of information—soft outputs, internal representations, relational structure—and because it composes naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and multi-teacher ensembles). When applied with attention to teacher quality, data alignment, and student pretraining, KD enables practical, resource-aware deployments across vision, speech, and language tasks. This paper argues KD should often be the first method considered for compression, and outlines core mechanisms, practical recipes, and remaining challenges for robust application in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Powerful, Context‑Dependent, and Best Used in Integrated Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When done beyond naïve soft-label copying—e.g., via intermediate-representation matching, attention or layer alignment, and careful teacher–student design—KD routinely delivers large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. Its strongest role is as a first-line, representation-aware strategy that is combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors and distributional failures. Practical deployment therefore requires principled recipes, diagnostics for failure modes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD succeeds when its objectives, representation targets, and training regimes are chosen to match deployment constraints and student capacity; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, data-free synthesis, and online protocols) extends its reach. However, KD also transfers risks (bias, privacy leakage, fragility) and faces limits when teacher signals are mismatched or training data are scarce, motivating task-aware design, robust distillation objectives, and emergent meta- and data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals—and are often combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). Across vision and language tasks, distillation commonly yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints are addressed. Important ongoing challenges include data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, robustness and fairness under compression, preserving rare-token behaviors in NLP, and principled choices about which signals to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Effective and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Risks, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large, high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. KD delivers large gains in inference speed and memory while preserving much of the teacher's utility across NLP tasks (including question answering and sentence understanding) and other modalities. However, naive distillation can transfer undesirable properties such as bias, privacy leakage, or fragility to distribution shift and adversarial attacks. A combination of strategies—student-aware teacher design, multi-teacher curricula, selective sample distillation, data augmentation, adversarial and robust distillation, and privacy-aware ensembles—provides a pragmatic path to compress models while controlling fairness, robustness, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Principled Use of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, practical method for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is conditional: choices about what to transfer, how to supervise internal representations, how to design student architectures for particular tasks, and how to handle data, distribution shift, and fairness constraints materially affect outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a flexible design pattern—combining soft-target transfer, internal-representation matching, task-adaptive architecture design, and explicit fairness or data strategies—to produce reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bishop
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Compression — Powerful but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven toolkit that forms the practical core of many model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs by transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals from large teachers to smaller students; however, real-world compression requires coordinated attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, robustness and fairness, and the complementary use of architectural and low-level compression techniques. Framing KD as a system‑level primitive and combining it with targeted interventions produces the most reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable tool for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. When combined with complementary practices — careful teacher selection or adaptation, pre-training of compact architectures, feature-level matching, and privacy- or data-aware workflows — KD yields most of the practical benefits of compression while exposing clear trade-offs and failure modes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the backbone of model compression pipelines, but that realizing reliable production gains requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact models by transferring richer supervision from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD encompasses multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational maps), supports various training regimes (offline teacher-to-student, online/co‑distillation, multi‑teacher ensembles), and composes with structural compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Its practical success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthetic-data strategies, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness. Treating KD as a design pipeline—selecting appropriate signals, aligning representations, adapting data strategies, and combining with complementary compression—yields students that meet real‑world deployment constraints while reducing common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach the performance of larger ones while meeting deployment constraints. KD methods vary in the form of transferred knowledge, how alignment is performed, and whether additional strategies (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) are used; empirical results show broad effectiveness across modalities but reveal important limitations and open problems around data availability, robustness, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language tasks. KD delivers compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and adaptations for data- or privacy-constrained settings. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, representations, attention maps), how to align teacher and student, and which data strategies and curricula to use. KD should therefore be treated as a first-line, system-level strategy in compression pipelines, but applied with explicit attention to context, complementary techniques, and evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Integrated Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, flexible means to produce compact models for deployment in compute-, memory-, or privacy-constrained settings. When chosen and applied with attention to what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits depend on principled design and evaluation, and it should be integrated into broader compression pipelines rather than used in isolation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger, higher-capacity teacher models into compact student models. KD methods span output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance, and data-aware or data-free training regimes. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation strategy is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. While distilled students frequently recover most of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, core challenges remain around distilling across heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, ensuring robustness and fairness, and operating when original training data are private or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the original performance. KD has proven effective across modalities and tasks, and modern practice extends beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, data-free approaches, and training-time strategies that make teachers more amenable to transfer. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: distribution shifts, limited or absent training data, teacher–student mismatch, and adversarial concerns require complementary techniques and careful design. When combined with task-aware selection of distilled signals, student-friendly teacher training, and data- or representation-aware remedies, KD becomes a practical backbone for deployment under latency, compute, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary strategies—pre-training compact architectures, feature-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis or augmentation, and task-aware student design—KD yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, and data availability; without such care, distillation can underperform or lose task-specific signals. I argue KD should be the first-line approach for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD should be treated as a first‑line strategy: it reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with capacity-aware student design, appropriate distilled signals, and complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure — its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks — so practitioners must apply KD as part of an integrated compression pipeline and evaluate its trade-offs in realistic deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically supported path to compress large models into compact, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central design pattern rather than a single loss term, KD enables multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and online schedules, and integration with architecture-aware design and other compression methods. Practical success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including pre-training of compact architectures and data augmentation or synthesis), and theoretical understanding of when soft versus hard supervision helps. Framed this way, KD is the most practical, multi-strategy mechanism for real-world compression, provided practitioners pair it with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Powerful, Context‑Dependent, and Best Used in Integrated Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When done beyond naïve soft-label copying—e.g., via intermediate-representation matching, attention or layer alignment, and careful teacher–student design—KD routinely delivers large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. Its strongest role is as a first-line, representation-aware strategy that is combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors and distributional failures. Practical deployment therefore requires principled recipes, diagnostics for failure modes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings, KD variants—ranging from logits or soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, many-to-many layer mapping, meta-learned teachers, data-free synthesis, and federated or device-aware schemes—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher utility. Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, choosing appropriate distillation targets and curricula, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Remaining gaps include optimization dynamics, data- and privacy-limited scenarios, theoretical explanations of when distillation helps, and robustness to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a practical, multi‑purpose toolkit that enables substantial efficiency gains when compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods—ranging from soft‑target matching to feature and attention imitation, multi‑teacher schedules, and data‑synthesis—regularly yield favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, but their real‑world success requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle limited or private data and distribution shifts.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate-feature alignment, attention and relational transfer, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Practical deployments typically combine KD with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies; remaining research challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving low-frequency or rare behaviors, privacy leakage, and principled automation of teacher/student design.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and effective strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. KD operates through multiple knowledge channels (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relations, and ensembles) and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data-free synthesis). While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and supports deployment under tight resource or privacy constraints, its success is context-dependent: teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and robustness or calibration requirements determine outcomes. Best practice treats KD as a design pipeline—choose task-appropriate transfer targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, leverage teacher ensembles or task-adaptive searches when helpful, and use data-aware or data-free methods where necessary.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and handling data- and deployment-specific constraints — KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, distillation is not automatic: outcomes depend on teacher strength and training, student architecture and capacity, the form of distilled signals, data availability (including data‑free settings), and fairness/privacy goals. Best practice treats KD as a core component combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and deployment-aware procedures to produce reliable, efficient models for real applications.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often ensemble or higher-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to improve accuracy, robustness, interpretability, or resource efficiency. Over the past decade KD has been adapted beyond the original soft-label logits transfer: methods now target intermediate features, attention maps, channel-wise signals, and training curricula; they address deployment constraints such as low-precision arithmetic, absence of original data, heterogeneous device models, and federated settings. In NLP, distillation has been applied to compress pretrained language models, to enable multi-task or lifelong learning, and to improve robustness in tasks such as question answering and machine translation. Practical recipes combine architectural adjustments, selective or staged distillation, and application-specific modifications to retain teacher strengths while avoiding transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-line, Context-aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, how intermediate layers are aligned, and whether data or privacy constraints hold, KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in inference speed and memory. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: optimization difficulties, mismatches in capacity between teacher and student, and limited or private data require tailored objectives, architecture-aware choices, and complementary techniques. This essay argues KD should be a primary strategy in model-compression toolkits while recommending concrete practices to increase reliability across real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Backbone with Bounded Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical strategy for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and, when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression techniques, yields efficient models suitable for latency- and memory-constrained deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design, and practitioners must address robustness, fairness, and task-specific constraints to realize reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants—has been developed to meet deployment constraints in vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows that, when combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though careful method selection is required to mitigate mismatches, data limitations, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The approach spans logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but its empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and training dynamics; open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, robustness, privacy, and heterogeneous architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) effectively compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus. KD has matured into a versatile toolkit that, when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and targeted objectives. Best practice therefore treats distillation as the central element of a compression pipeline, augmented by augmentation, curriculum design, privacy-aware aggregation, and architecture-aware substitution to mitigate known failure modes and preserve robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Favoring Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, versatile pathway to produce compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a design paradigm—choosing what form of knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs across modalities. KD should be adopted as the default first‑line compression method in deep learning and NLP while being applied with careful safeguards for data, robustness, and task alignment.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses a family of techniques — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or token-level signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation variants, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches — and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) to meet deployment constraints. Practical success requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, the provenance and availability of distillation data, and careful objective and schedule design; open challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, avoiding propagation of biases or privacy leakage, and ensuring robustness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile paradigm for transferring knowledge from larger or more informative teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods extend beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and matched to deployment constraints, KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes dominant mechanisms, common variants, practical guidance, representative applications, and open challenges for KD-driven model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone for Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible toolkit for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free training. When combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design, KD produces practical accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for vision, language, and multimodal systems. However, the method’s success is context-dependent: it requires attention to teacher quality and bias, student capacity and architecture compatibility, data provenance and synthesis, and robustness under distributional shift. This synthesis argues that KD should be treated as a central, system-level primitive in compression pipelines but implemented with task-aware choices and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Primary, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation signals (logits, features, attention), accounting for teacher–student capacity, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency burdens while enabling deployment across edge, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, KD is not a universal cure: its benefits depend on optimization, data availability, and robustness/fairness goals, and practical deployments require matching KD variants to constraints and verifying student behavior under distribution shift and adversarial threats.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of methods—logit (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- or module-alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, progressive module replacement, online distillation, and data-free generative approaches—has been developed to address different deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices). Empirical work shows these techniques can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, what is transferred, data availability, and task-specific alignment. Open challenges include robust transfer of rare-token behaviors, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and scaling distillation to privacy- and resource-constrained or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Focused Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for producing compact models by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students. Methods extend beyond matching softened output distributions to include intermediate-feature imitation, attention or relational alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or synthetic-data procedures. Best practices combine representation-aware objectives, student-aware architecture choices, and data strategies (pretraining, augmentation, or synthetic data) and often pair KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work across vision, speech, and NLP demonstrates KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but known limitations remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, robustness, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. Its practical success depends strongly on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (or plausible synthetic surrogates), and integration with complementary compression primitives such as pruning and quantization. KD is therefore best treated as a context-dependent component of compression pipelines rather than a single recipe; doing so enables robust, efficient models for a wide range of deep-learning and NLP applications while revealing clear directions for research on heterogeneity, rare-token behavior, and privacy-preserving transfer.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD methods cover matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware variants (including data-free and few-shot approaches). In practice KD is usually combined with architecture-aware choices (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data or synthetic-data strategies. While KD often yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, the chosen distillation signals, and data provenance; persistent challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preserving low-frequency behaviors, and avoiding transfer of undesirable biases. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical recommendations, and open problems for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or synthetic data, and they are often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. While KD routinely produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, its effectiveness depends on careful choices about the distilled signals, teacher–student compatibility, data provenance (including data-free settings), and training regimes to preserve robustness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of distillation objectives—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention- and channel-guided losses, relational/contrastive signals, and self- or multi-teacher regimes—can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity, access to (or synthesis of) suitable training data, and mitigation of optimization, fairness, and robustness risks. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative methods, practical recommendations, and open challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade a diverse family of distillation methods has emerged—logit-level soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, multi-teacher ensembles, and privacy-aware adaptations—applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data availability and domain mismatch; combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture search, quantization) and task-aware pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical, flexible, and widely applied approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and language tasks. KD brings together soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware strategies into a single, adaptable pipeline that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet real-world deployment constraints. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs, its reliability depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these concerns makes KD a central component of robust, system-level compression workflows rather than a one-shot recipe.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single compression trick but a flexible set of techniques that can reduce model size, preserve or transfer task-relevant information, enable deployment in latency- and memory-constrained settings, support domain adaptation and privacy-preserving federated workflows, and be combined with structural compression. When applied thoughtfully — with task-aware selection of distilled signals, architecturally informed teacher-student design, and attention to data availability and optimization dynamics — KD yields large practical benefits for deep learning and NLP systems while avoiding common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical toolkit for turning large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Methods vary from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, optimization choices, and targeted handling of robustness, low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive settings. Important open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, preserving rare-token and domain-specific signals, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers or data are scarce, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Outcomes, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal signals from teachers. Over the past decade KD has broadened from simple soft-label matching to a diverse set of techniques — intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data- or generator-based synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems remain in robustness to domain shift, preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks, privacy- and data-constrained distillation, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and targeted objectives; therefore KD should be treated as a first-line tool that must be adapted to the deployment context rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

papers_seen.author: Garcia

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.
