papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely used family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" models so that students approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive signals, and it is often combined with architecture modification, pruning, quantization, and data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data approaches). Empirical and conceptual work shows KD reliably improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, graph, and cross-domain tasks, but its success is context dependent: teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, availability and domain match of data, and explicit handling of robustness, privacy, and distribution shift are central determinants of outcome.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, methods include soft-target (logit) distillation, feature and representation matching, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained models, data- and privacy-aware protocols, and training-time variants such as online or co-distillation. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance while yielding substantial savings in memory, latency, and energy; however, outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, access to task data, which signals are transferred, and training protocol choices. Key open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, handling teacher errors and low-frequency phenomena, and reducing distillation cost when teachers are large or data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible supervision (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensemble signals) and interoperates with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data synthesis). When used systematically—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, leveraging data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployments. At the same time, careful attention to teacher quality, rare-token preservation, robustness, and domain shift is required to avoid predictable failure modes and to maximize real-world utility.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD succeeds across modalities when treated as a design pipeline that combines what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints and deployment constraints (privacy, latency, heterogeneity). KD is powerful but not universally sufficient: realizing its benefits requires co-design of teacher and student, complementary compression techniques, and safeguards for low-frequency phenomena, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational technique for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. When applied thoughtfully — combining representational objectives, teacher-student co-design, task-aware compression, and appropriate data strategies — KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining robustness and fairness. However, pitfalls arise from mismatches in inputs, teacher strength, data availability, and dataset biases; practical KD should therefore be integrated with complementary methods (e.g., architecture search, pruning, curriculum strategies, and data-generation) and with safeguards for ethical concerns.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Compression, Regularization, and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression heuristic into a versatile training paradigm that enables model size reduction, improved generalization, domain adaptation, and task consolidation. Its practical success depends on both the sources of teacher supervision (final logits, intermediate representations, or multiple teachers) and how distillation is applied (sample selection, layer matching, or label design). While KD frequently yields compact, high-performing models, its benefits arise from a mixture of transferred dark knowledge and regularizing effects of soft targets; careful design choices are required to realize those benefits across settings such as language model compression, multi-task training, and privacy-constrained or heterogeneous environments.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language tasks. KD delivers compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and adaptations for data- or privacy-constrained settings. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, representations, attention maps), how to align teacher and student, and which data strategies and curricula to use. KD should therefore be treated as a first-line, system-level strategy in compression pipelines, but applied with explicit attention to context, complementary techniques, and evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. A broad family of KD methods transfers teacher behavior through soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- or task-aware layer projection, ensemble/online schemes, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. When combined with architecture search, progressive module replacement, or data synthesis, KD enables strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs that make large pretrained models practical for edge, federated, and privacy-sensitive deployments. Key practical decisions include what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align mismatched teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or no access to original training data. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student compatibility, data heterogeneity, robustness under compression, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so that deployments meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structures; they can be applied in offline, online, or multi-teacher regimes and combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability (including data-free or federated settings), and careful selection of distillation targets and training curricula. Remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, distribution shift, preservation of rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful, pragmatic approach for shrinking large models into deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. When combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization) and student-aware curricula, KD frequently achieves large reductions in memory and latency while retaining most of teacher performance. However, realizing these gains in production requires careful attention to what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—soft logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational signals—to enable substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much teacher performance. Its success in practice depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and complementary compression methods. KD is powerful but not universal: optimization mismatch, domain shift, and limited data can undermine transfer, so robust pipelines co-design student architectures, distillation signals, and training/data workflows to realize production gains.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and teacher-free/self-distillation variants. KD is most effective when treated as a system-level design choice—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost with modest performance loss, its success depends on data availability, optimization dynamics, teacher quality, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness; open challenges remain around domain shift, preserving rare-token behaviors in language models, privacy-aware distillation, and principled data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) supervision to include intermediate feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, and handling data availability or provenance; open problems include principled teacher design, robust data-free approaches, preserving long-tail or safety-critical behaviors, and theoretical characterization of when particular knowledge sources help.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, versatile approach for shrinking large models into compact students that are deployable under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. Its success depends on treating distillation not as a single loss but as a system design choice: selecting what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relations), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, what data or synthetic surrogates to use, and which complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to combine. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains in many settings but is context-dependent: careful choices about teacher quality, data availability, and objective design are required to avoid failure modes such as capacity mismatch, degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena, or privacy/robustness tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have diversified from the original logits-based teacher→student paradigm into a broad set of methods that operate on features, modules, data, and training procedures. Contemporary work shows multiple complementary mechanisms for transferring knowledge—soft targets, feature- and attention-level mimicry, adversarial alignment, module replacement, and data- or communication-constrained distillation—each suited to different deployment constraints (privacy, compute, bandwidth) and model families (transformers, CNNs, GANs, GNNs). Advances emphasize (1) understanding why KD helps (stability, richer concept learning), (2) designing where to transfer knowledge (penultimate features, attention maps, projectors), and (3) tailoring the distillation process to practical settings (online multi-model training, federated environments, data-free scenarios, and teacher models optimized for students). Empirical results across vision, speech, language, generation, and retrieval indicate KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance when the distillation objective, the representation level, and the training dynamics are appropriately matched to the target constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans algorithmic advances in teacher–student objectives, architecture-aware compression, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Practical work shows gains from combining KD with data augmentation, many-to-many layer mappings, and architecture search, while complementary efforts address data-free and privacy-preserving distillation. Remaining challenges include imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, and adapting compression to task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from logits-based soft-target matching to a rich family of techniques including feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and representation matching, student-aware teacher design, and integration with architecture search and other compression primitives. Empirical work across vision and language shows KD both as a route to practical deployment of pre-trained transformers and as a general regularizer that can improve student generalization; ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, coping with limited or private data, and preserving performance on rare classes or tokens. This article synthesizes core methods, mechanistic explanations, practical adaptations for NLP, and directions where KD currently has the greatest impact.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—has proven effective across vision, language, and other modalities. Practical success depends on co-designing what is transferred, student architecture and capacity, and data strategies; important open problems include robust transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, data-free and privacy-sensitive distillation, and principled combinations of KD with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. When treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss term, KD can be adapted to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch to produce compact models that retain much of teachers' performance. Practical application of KD involves choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to expose students to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online predictions), and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods and privacy-preserving protocols. Despite strong empirical success, KD has known failure modes tied to teacher errors, limited data, and distribution shift that require targeted mitigations and principled design.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential and Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but its reliability depends on choices about what to distill, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited, heterogeneous, or private data. Realistic deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, adapting the distillation signal to the task and student capacity, and evaluating robustness and privacy implications.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students) to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining task performance. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or structural signals), how teachers and students are aligned (layer mappings, many-to-many correspondences), how data is used (original training data, synthetic or generated data, or no data), and how multiple teachers or online training regimes are incorporated. KD is routinely combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and used across vision, language, graph, and generative-model settings. Empirical and practical work shows KD can produce compact models suitable for deployment, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful design of distillation objectives and training curricula.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically validated strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through a range of mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, teacher ensembles, and data‑side interventions) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and deployment constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, practitioners must treat it as a context‑sensitive tool and follow best practices to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or encountering failure modes under limited data, heterogeneity, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Compression Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP: Rationale and Practical Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, first‑line strategy for compressing large neural models in deep learning and NLP because it provides flexible, task‑aware transfer channels that preserve predictive behavior while enabling complementary structural compression. KD excels when combined with architecture-aware design, representation-level alignment, and data strategies that address limited or private training data. A practical KD-first pipeline—selecting appropriate transfer signals, applying task-aware layer mappings, leveraging data-free or augmentation methods when needed, and composing KD with pruning/quantization—yields robust, high-compression students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models so the students can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a broad family of objectives that include intermediate representation matching, attention- and relational-level transfer, ensemble-to-single distillation, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. In practice KD is most effective when its signals are chosen to match student capacity and the deployment setting, and when it is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data strategies. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior (especially in NLP), aligning heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models while attempting to preserve accuracy and useful inductive biases. Approaches span classic teacher–student logit matching, representation and feature imitation, layer mapping strategies for large pretrained language models, data-free and zero-shot methods that avoid access to original training data, and privacy- or communication-aware frameworks for distributed settings. Empirical work demonstrates these methods can yield practical speedups, substantial parameter reductions, and competitive task performance across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks; theoretical and empirical studies also clarify when softened teacher targets or distilled datasets best help student capacity. Remaining challenges include balancing privacy and utility, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers are large, and extending guarantees and methods across modalities and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques that transfers information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or feature distributions, and can be combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) or data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and provenance of data, and robustness to distributional shifts. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as one element of a broader compression toolkit and apply task- and deployment-aware design choices to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers behaviors of larger or differently structured models into smaller or alternative models by training students to match teacher outputs, intermediate representations, or other derived supervision signals. Empirically, distillation improves deployment efficiency, can transfer inductive biases and robustness properties, and enables compression across domains including classification, generation, speech, and transformers. Success depends on choices such as what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or synthetic labels), how to combine hard and soft targets, privacy/robustness constraints, and whether teachers are perfect. Contemporary work links distillation to regularization and label smoothing, proposes layer-level and adversarial methods, and demonstrates broad applicability while highlighting limitations tied to teacher quality, data distribution, and adversarial vulnerability.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. KD methods differ in what is transferred (softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational signals) and in training protocols (offline teacher supervision, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants). In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when practitioner choices account for teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and target-task constraints. While KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, its limitations include sensitivity to optimization dynamics, degradation on rare or safety-critical behaviors, and challenges in data-free or privacy-constrained settings. The field offers pragmatic recipes—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning representations, and using data or synthetic surrogates—that produce deployable compact models, but outstanding research questions remain about principled teacher design, robustness under distribution shift, and data-free distillation quality.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Flexible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. When treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, distillation enables compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Combining KD with representation-aware objectives, teacher–student design, and deployment-aware techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, or federated protocols) addresses many real-world constraints while leaving open research questions about data-free distillation, cross-architecture representation transfer, and domain-generalization under aggressive compression.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a unifying, practical framework to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while addressing concerns of computation, privacy, robustness, and limited task data. KD techniques span from logits- and feature-based matching to progressive module replacement, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free (zero-shot) synthesis, and federated output-sharing, and when combined with careful data augmentation and generative replay they yield compact models that retain much of the teacher utility in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware adaptations; in practice it is combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies. While KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs, its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, and targeted handling of robustness, low-frequency behaviour, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A spectrum of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational patterns) and training regimes (offline teacher-to-student, online co-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis) enables practical trade-offs between performance, latency, and memory. Effective compression usually combines distillation with architecture-aware choices and complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability; remaining challenges include distribution shift, preserving rare-token and domain-specific behavior, privacy-aware distillation, and reducing the computational cost of distillation itself.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD encompasses a range of transferred signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational patterns, and ensemble outputs), operates under multiple training regimes (offline, online, multi‑teacher, and data‑free), and composes naturally with structural compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, speech, and language shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and attention to robustness, rare-token preservation, and fairness. Open challenges include reliable data‑free distillation, principled signal selection for heterogeneous architectures, and preserving safety‑critical behaviours under compression.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language processing. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students using a variety of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and configurations (single- or multi-teacher, online/offline, data-driven or data-free). When combined with complementary compression techniques and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models with substantially reduced inference cost while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, the type and availability of data used for transfer, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness, and so KD is best applied as one element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has diversified from matching soft logits to a family of techniques that include intermediate feature and attention imitation, projector- or layer-aware mapping, ensemble and curriculum strategies, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants. Practical pipelines typically combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic examples) to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints, while facing challenges from teacher–student mismatch, data availability, and robustness or bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Conditional, Pipeline‑Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD routinely yields students that approach teacher performance across tasks when practitioners attend to what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data are handled. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design. I argue that KD should be treated as the practical core or first‑line strategy for model compression, but only when it is applied as part of a careful pipeline that combines complementary compression techniques, explicit robustness and fairness checks, and data-aware distillation practices.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Capability, Mechanisms, and Bounded Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for converting large, high‑performance models into compact students that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. When designers choose appropriate distilled signals, align teacher and student capacities, and combine KD with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a universal solution: its benefits depend on teacher quality and compatibility, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, long‑tail behaviors, and deployment constraints. This paper argues that KD should serve as a practical core of compression pipelines while being applied judiciously and in combination with other techniques to address known limits.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Central, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD methods span soft‑label/ logits transfer, intermediate‑feature and attention matching, adversarial and data‑free approaches, and teacher‑student co‑training or meta‑learned teachers. When thoughtfully designed — selecting appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student capacities, and addressing data availability and robustness requirements — KD enables practical deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. However, KD is not universally successful: its effectiveness depends on architecture compatibility, quality and coverage of data (or of synthetic surrogates), and task‑specific choices, so practitioners must evaluate distillation under realistic conditions and adopt best practices tailored to their constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Pragmatic Design Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable family of methods that enables deployment of high-performing but resource-hungry models by training compact students that retain much of teacher behavior. KD delivers major operational benefits — reduced inference latency, lower memory footprint, and greater deployability under compute, bandwidth, and privacy constraints — but it is not a one-size-fits-all cure. Real-world success requires treating KD as a design paradigm: choose what form of knowledge to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), co-design teacher and student capacities, address data limitations (via targeted augmentation or synthetic data), and explicitly manage robustness, fairness, and rare-token behaviors. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful evaluation, KD is the central practical strategy for producing efficient, reliable models for modern NLP and deep-learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. Across vision and NLP, KD methods extend beyond logit matching to include intermediate-representation imitation, attention and relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-constrained or data-free procedures. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines—especially when combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, or quantization—regularly yield compact models that recover much of the teacher’s performance, though open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, fairness, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller or otherwise constrained models. Approaches span from matching outputs to mimicking intermediate representations, from layer-aware mapping strategies to task-adaptive architecture search, and include protocols for heterogeneous, data-constrained, or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical results across vision and language tasks demonstrate strong gains in efficiency with modest drops (or even improvements) in performance, while persistent challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, choosing appropriate sources of knowledge, and designing robust data-free or federated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD mechanisms — soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and task- or deployment-aware pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in inference cost, but success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and task-specific considerations (e.g., preserving fine-grained sequence behavior or relational structure). Privacy, heterogeneity of deployment devices, and data-scarce regimes motivate variants with differential privacy, few-shot or cross-layer schemes, and heterogeneous multi-model sharing to ensure inclusive and practical compression.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization, KD reliably improves accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Success requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, the nature and provenance of distillation data, and evaluation for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy. KD is therefore best treated as a first-line, system-level primitive for compression rather than a universal cure: with careful design it yields high-impact, deployable compact models, but its limits must be managed through targeted engineering and auditing.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Dependent Core for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and provenance, and explicit strategies to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or failing on low-frequency phenomena. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a central tool within an integrated compression strategy, tuned to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, deployable models (students), or otherwise reduce network size while retaining performance. Approaches range from matching final predictions to aligning intermediate representations, and they address practical constraints such as limited data, privacy, device heterogeneity, and robustness. Recent work spans algorithmic mechanisms (soft targets, layer mapping, adversarial sample synthesis), application-specific pipelines (BERT compression, non-autoregressive translation, task-adaptive models), and theoretical interpretations that link distillation to regularization. This synthesis summarizes core techniques, practical extensions, and open challenges reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings, KD variants—ranging from logits or soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, many-to-many layer mapping, meta-learned teachers, data-free synthesis, and federated or device-aware schemes—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher utility. Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, choosing appropriate distillation targets and curricula, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Remaining gaps include optimization dynamics, data- and privacy-limited scenarios, theoretical explanations of when distillation helps, and robustness to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving predictive performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, contrastive and relational signals, online or teacher-free co-training, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data availability; remaining challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and reliable distillation when original data are limited or private.
