papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides flexible supervision signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention patterns) that enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability, and task specificity. Realistic deployment therefore requires combining KD with complementary strategies (task-aware layer selection, architecture search, data augmentation or synthesis, multi-teacher schemes, and privacy-aware mechanisms) and evaluating tradeoffs under the target constraints.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably yields compact models that retain much of a larger teacher’s performance when applied with attention to what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability. KD works through multiple mechanisms—soft-target regularization, representation transfer, and ensemble-derived ‘‘dark knowledge’’—and its strengths are maximized when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware training curricula. However, KD is not a universal solution: practical deployments must address limits including distribution shift, rare-token behavior, privacy-sensitive or data-free scenarios, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher behavior. I therefore argue that KD should be treated as the practical core of hybrid compression pipelines, selected and tuned according to deployment constraints and supplemented with methods that mitigate its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically grounded approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely produces favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when practitioners choose what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, relational signals), align teacher and student architectures, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on data availability, teacher quality and design, teacher–student compatibility, and evaluation under distribution shift and fairness constraints. Responsible deployment therefore requires principled choices about distilled signals, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When used as a system-level strategy—choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely delivers favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory in vision and language tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: data availability, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, and robustness or fairness concerns limit what a distilled student can inherit reliably. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the default first-line method within a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, data strategies (including data-free or privacy-aware approaches), and explicit evaluation for rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance characteristics from larger models. Research has introduced multiple KD paradigms—teacher-student soft-label transfer, self-distillation, feature/internal-representation matching, multi-teacher strategies, and data-augmentation–aware distillation—each addressing different practical constraints such as domain shift, resource limits, or heterogeneous architectures. Applications span speech, machine translation evaluation, ASR, and domain-specific pretrained models; empirical work shows substantial reductions in model size and latency can be achieved with modest accuracy loss, or sometimes even gains, when distillation is combined with architectural adaptations and training-time strategies. Remaining challenges include transferring internal representations across heterogeneous architectures, choosing or designing teachers that are most useful for particular students, and preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals during aggressive compression.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive power. The approach spans simple logit matching to richer supervision such as intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial and online schemes, curriculum-driven supervision, and multi-teacher or self-distillation variants. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks, but its success depends on what is transferred, the data used for distillation, and procedures that preserve robustness and domain generalization. Key challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, data scarcity or absence, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate-feature alignment, attention and relational transfer, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Practical deployments typically combine KD with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies; remaining research challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving low-frequency or rare behaviors, privacy leakage, and principled automation of teacher/student design.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses a spectrum of techniques—from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals—and is often combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical results across vision, language, healthcare, and graph domains show KD can recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and evaluation under realistic deployment conditions. Important open problems include data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, principled selection of teacher signals, robustness and fairness under compression, and methods that scale distillation quality and efficiency together.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. A broad family of KD techniques—ranging from softened-logit supervision to intermediate representation matching, attention- and feature-level imitation, many-to-many layer alignment, adversarial and data-free variants, and task- or device-aware architecture search—enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often retaining most of the teacher's performance. Effective application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, whether and how to use original data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Important open problems remain regarding theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift or imperfect teachers, and scalable private or data-free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep-learning models into smaller, deployable students. When designed and applied carefully, KD reduces inference latency, memory footprint, and deployment cost while preserving much of a teacher model’s performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what information is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Treating KD as a design paradigm—co-designing teachers and students, selecting appropriate distillation signals, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—yields the most reliable path to efficient models in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central model-compression approach that trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost, memory, and deployment barriers are reduced while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive behavior. Research has produced a family of distillation objectives (soft-targets, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational losses), training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation, multi-teacher), and system-level integrations (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical studies show well-designed distillation pipelines commonly recover a large fraction of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, but success depends on what knowledge is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical use therefore combines algorithmic choices with architecture-aware compression and data strategies tailored to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and natural language processing. The family of KD methods spans soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate representation and attention imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online or co-distillation schemes. Successful application requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, whether original data are available (or must be synthesized), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical practice shows KD frequently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but open problems remain around robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, theoretical understanding of transfer dynamics, and scalable private or data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded toolkit that enables compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when paired with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods. However, its effectiveness is context-dependent: success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy concerns. Treating KD as the backbone of an integrated compression pipeline delivers the best practical outcomes while acknowledging and mitigating its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed not as a single trick but as a central, system-level toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student co-design, suitable data strategies (including synthesis or data-free protocols), and deployment-aware training schedules, KD yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability; it also raises risks around transferring biases, losing rare-token behaviors, and underperforming under distribution shift. Treating KD as a first-line, flexible approach within a broader compression pipeline — rather than a one-size-fits-all cure — produces the most reliable outcomes for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including domain adaptation and black-box/data-free workflows). In practice KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures, combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and tailored to data availability and deployment constraints. Despite wide empirical success across vision and NLP, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, distilling rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable compression when training data are limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, But Not the Whole, of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD scales across modalities and deployment regimes, enabling latency-, memory-, and communication-constrained applications. However, distillation is not a drop-in cure: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and students are co-designed, the availability and provenance of data, and safeguards for fairness, robustness, and privacy. A pragmatic stance treats KD as a system-level primitive that should be combined with complementary techniques (data synthesis, representation matching, multi-teacher curricula, and privacy-aware ensembles) to realize reliable, efficient models in real-world NLP and deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from pre-trained teachers. The approach spans soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical results show KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and optimization protocols. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, maintaining robustness and fairness under distribution shift, and operating when original training data is limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad set of practical recipes—including logit (soft-target) supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and joint use with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—enable deployment of compact models across vision, language, and graph tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while reducing compute and memory, but effectiveness depends on the choice of transfer target, availability or synthesis of suitable data, student architecture, and training dynamics. Key open issues remain around principled explanations for when distillation helps, reliably transferring robustness and fairness properties, privacy-aware distillation, and automating student design for specific resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers in both vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints, and many variants extend KD beyond soft-target transfer to feature matching, multi-teacher schemes, progressive replacement, and domain-adaptive workflows. At the same time, theoretical and empirical analyses reveal optimization barriers, sensitivity to the choice of data and teacher signals, and imperfect matching between teacher and student as important limits. This review argues that KD is a powerful but context-dependent tool: its success requires matching the distillation signal to student capacity and task complexity, combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and paying careful attention to data and training dynamics to avoid degenerate outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free synthesis—has been developed and frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical results across vision and NLP show that carefully designed distillation pipelines recover much of the teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but persistent challenges remain in handling data scarcity or privacy constraints, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student capacities, and preserving robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring useful predictive and representational knowledge from teacher models to students. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-teacher weighting, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization) and guided by student-aware design and fairness/robustness constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of a teacher's accuracy. Practical deployment of KD requires attention to data availability, teacher quality, and domain-specific constraints to avoid propagating undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple logit matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data- and communication-constrained protocols, and progressive module replacement. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and training protocols. Important open issues include robust transfer under distribution shift, efficient distillation when teacher cost is high, and preserving fairness and safety properties in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD methods cover matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware variants (including data-free and few-shot approaches). In practice KD is usually combined with architecture-aware choices (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data or synthetic-data strategies. While KD often yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, the chosen distillation signals, and data provenance; persistent challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preserving low-frequency behaviors, and avoiding transfer of undesirable biases. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical recommendations, and open problems for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. A spectrum of KD strategies has been developed—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, self-distillation, and data-free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows well-designed distillation pipelines can recover much of a teacher’s performance while delivering large gains in latency and memory, but outcomes depend on the choice of distillation signal, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints such as domain shift and privacy. Current practical directions emphasize representation-aware objectives, layer-alignment techniques, and hybrid pipelines that treat KD as a core element of system-level compression.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models. Methods range from matching teacher outputs (soft logits) to supervising intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and may be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across modalities, but practical success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness to domain shift, and choices about what form of knowledge to distill.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-Line, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, practical starting point for compressing large models because it provides flexible, task‑aware mechanisms to transfer behavior from high-capacity teachers to efficient students. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute when combined with targeted design choices. However, its success depends on what signals are distilled, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and domain constraints; therefore KD must be integrated into a broader, context‑adapted compression pipeline rather than used as a blind one‑size‑fits‑all fix.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring useful information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, faster, or more constrained models (students). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of the teacher's predictive performance. Approaches extend beyond matching final logits to include representation- and attention-level supervision, layer-mapping strategies, multi-teacher ensembles, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. Practical deployment combines KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires attention to data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and task constraints. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, distilling under limited or private data, and ensuring robust transfer of inductive biases and safety properties.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger, higher-capacity teacher models into compact student models. KD methods span output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance, and data-aware or data-free training regimes. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation strategy is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. While distilled students frequently recover most of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, core challenges remain around distilling across heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, ensuring robustness and fairness, and operating when original training data are private or unavailable.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted strategy for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD has been adapted into a family of techniques that vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), how transfer is scheduled (offline, online, multi-teacher), and how data constraints are handled (real-data, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). In practice, KD is most effective when treated as a system-level design primitive and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, student-aware architecture design) and data strategies, but its success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. The literature describes a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi‑teacher) and data strategies (original data, augmented or synthetic data, and data‑free variants). KD is frequently combined with architectural or precision changes such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and deployment constraints including privacy and robustness. Best practices treat distillation as a system-level pipeline that integrates pretraining, tailored distillation objectives, and complementary compression techniques to achieve reliable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs in real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Bishop
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Compression — Powerful but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven toolkit that forms the practical core of many model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs by transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals from large teachers to smaller students; however, real-world compression requires coordinated attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, robustness and fairness, and the complementary use of architectural and low-level compression techniques. Framing KD as a system‑level primitive and combining it with targeted interventions produces the most reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a pipeline—combining choice of distillation targets, student architecture design, pretraining, data strategies, and complementary compression steps—KD yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP. Yet KD is context-dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, availability and provenance of training data, and explicit design to preserve rare-token or domain-specific behavior. I argue KD should be the default first‑line method for model compression in deep learning and NLP while practitioners remain attentive to its failure modes and incorporate multi-teacher, domain‑aware, and data-aware remedies where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of distillation objectives—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention- and channel-guided losses, relational/contrastive signals, and self- or multi-teacher regimes—can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity, access to (or synthesis of) suitable training data, and mitigation of optimization, fairness, and robustness risks. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative methods, practical recommendations, and open challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single loss term, KD reliably improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities and tasks. Its success depends on deliberate choices about what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. Important open problems remain around distribution shift, low-frequency behaviors, privacy- and data-constrained settings, and principled data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile technique for shrinking large neural models while preserving much of their predictive power. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, distillation enables faster inference, reduced memory footprint, and easier deployment in latency- and resource-constrained settings. When combined with teacher ensembles, online or self-distillation, task-adaptive search, and careful handling of soft labels and data augmentation, distillation can deliver near-teacher accuracy while addressing scalability, robustness, and domain transfer concerns. I argue that knowledge distillation should be a first-line approach for model compression in modern NLP pipelines, supplemented by principled choices about teachers, data, and optimization to realize its full benefits.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals—and are often combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). Across vision and language tasks, distillation commonly yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints are addressed. Important ongoing challenges include data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, robustness and fairness under compression, preserving rare-token behaviors in NLP, and principled choices about which signals to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: The Pragmatic Power and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured into a practical toolkit for shrinking models, transferring behavior across architectures and modalities, and enabling deployment under compute, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond straightforward teacher-to-student compression, distillation techniques combine with data augmentation, synthetic-data generation, and regularization to address limited data, cross-domain gaps, and interpretability needs. However, outcomes depend on choices about teacher quality, training data availability, and objective design; careful method selection is required to realize reliable, production-ready gains.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include soft-output (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, and more recent data-free, multi-teacher, and online/self-distillation variants. When combined with architecture-aware transformations such as pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search, KD enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory that are critical for deploying NLP systems. Remaining challenges include distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and fine-grained behaviors, robustness under distribution shift and adversarial settings, and safeguarding fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment and adaptation in deep learning and NLP. When combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; at the same time, careful method choice is required to avoid pitfalls such as degraded rare-token behavior, transferred biases, and failures under limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, but conditional, strategy for model compression and provides concrete recommendations for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Bradshaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer aspects of teacher behavior—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, availability of (or access to) data, and careful design of distillation objectives and training curricula. Open problems include robust transfer under domain shift, reliable data-free distillation, preservation of rare or safety-critical behaviors, and principled co-design of teacher and student for deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multi‑Strategy, Practical — but Bounded — Path for Compressing Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. When applied thoughtfully — combining soft-label transfer with representation-level guidance, architecture-aware design, and data strategies — KD enables compact models that meet memory, latency, and deployment constraints while retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: limited or private data, teacher errors, student capacity gaps, and robustness or fairness concerns create concrete failure modes that require complementary methods and careful evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a multi-strategy engineering approach whose best results arise from combining several targeted techniques that suit task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has diversified from matching soft logits to a family of techniques that include intermediate feature and attention imitation, projector- or layer-aware mapping, ensemble and curriculum strategies, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants. Practical pipelines typically combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic examples) to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints, while facing challenges from teacher–student mismatch, data availability, and robustness or bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks KD uses multiple transfer channels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and training regimes (offline teacher supervision, online co-training, multi-teacher ensembles) to recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory. Practical deployments typically combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and must manage data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, and robustness to domain shift and rare behaviors. Remaining challenges concern data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, principled choices of which teacher signals to transfer for a given student and task, and avoiding transfer of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students retain much of the teachers’ functionality while being cheaper to run. KD operates through multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation). In practice KD is most effective when treated as a system-level pipeline that reconciles teacher–student mismatches, leverages appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized), and combines with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). The method reliably improves deployment trade-offs in many settings, but its success is context-dependent: it is sensitive to teacher quality and alignment, data availability and provenance, student capacity, and distributional or privacy constraints. Open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of teacher performance. Research across vision, speech, translation, and NLP tasks has developed multiple KD objectives (soft logits, intermediate-feature matching, attention or projector-based alignment), training regimes (offline teacher–student, self-distillation, multi-teacher, adversarial transfer), and data strategies (data-free, distilled datasets, and hybrid authentic/synthetic training). Empirical and theoretical work explains why KD often improves student generalization (dark-knowledge regularization, transferred inductive biases) while also documenting limitations (capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, distributional/low-frequency failures) and practical remedies. Best practice is to treat KD as a flexible toolkit and combine it with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.
