papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or multi-modal models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural insights. Research has developed diverse KD variants—soft-label distillation, internal and layer-wise imitation, task-aware filtering, data-free distillation, and architecture-search guided compression—each addressing optimization, data availability, or deployment constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between matching teacher outputs and student generalization, the value of pre-training compact models, and the importance of choosing what and how knowledge is transferred to maximize downstream task performance while meeting resource limits.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical tool for compressing large models into efficient students while acknowledging that its effectiveness depends critically on task, data, teacher–student alignment, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data strategies), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, but reliable production use requires deliberate signal selection, capacity-aware alignment, and privacy- or data-sensitive adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from pre-trained teachers. The approach spans soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical results show KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and optimization protocols. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, maintaining robustness and fairness under distribution shift, and operating when original training data is limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher to student. A diverse set of approaches extend the basic soft-label paradigm to include internal representation matching, layer-wise and attention-guided alignment, task-aware selection of distilled features, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, augmentation-driven consistency, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, adversarial learning objectives, and architecture search tailored to downstream tasks. These techniques improve inference efficiency while aiming to preserve accuracy, generalization, and task-specific behavior; they also enable distillation in settings with limited or no access to original training data and in generation tasks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, selecting which teacher knowledge to preserve for a given student capacity and task, and designing robust distilled models that generalize across domains and data shifts.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Synthesizing Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students so that deployed systems meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a family of mechanisms — soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, relation- or attention-based transfer, and data-side interventions — that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical results show that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and augmentation, architecture compatibility, and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated pathway to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD encompasses multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and operates across modes (offline, online, ensemble, data-free). When co‑designed with student architectures and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for vision and language models. However, practical success requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, and robustness to domain shift and rare behaviors. The method is best treated as a default, context‑aware tool that should be adapted—rather than assumed universal—for each deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical results across vision, language, generation, and specialized domains show that KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling substantial improvements in latency, memory footprint, and privacy-sensitive deployment. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success hinges on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to align teacher and student representations, how to handle limited or private data, and whether robustness or task-specific constraints must be preserved. Treating KD as a pipeline and co-designing teacher, student, objectives, and data/augmentation yields the most reliable practical gains.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so that deployments meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structures; they can be applied in offline, online, or multi-teacher regimes and combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability (including data-free or federated settings), and careful selection of distillation targets and training curricula. Remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, distribution shift, preservation of rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including domain adaptation and black-box/data-free workflows). In practice KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures, combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and tailored to data availability and deployment constraints. Despite wide empirical success across vision and NLP, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, distilling rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable compression when training data are limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models. Methods range from matching teacher outputs (soft logits) to supervising intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and may be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across modalities, but practical success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness to domain shift, and choices about what form of knowledge to distill.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large, high-performance models into smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Recent work spans many complementary strategies — logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer-wise distillation, structural and channel-level transformations, data-free generation of proxy inputs, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and task-aware filtering — and addresses practical concerns such as cross-domain transfer, limited compute, and maintaining task performance in NLP settings. Progress includes specialized algorithms for pre-trained language model compression, algorithmic and architectural enhancements that reduce capacity gaps, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Together these developments offer a toolkit for deploying compact models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive environments while preserving most of the original model performance.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Focused Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for producing compact models by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students. Methods extend beyond matching softened output distributions to include intermediate-feature imitation, attention or relational alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or synthetic-data procedures. Best practices combine representation-aware objectives, student-aware architecture choices, and data strategies (pretraining, augmentation, or synthetic data) and often pair KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work across vision, speech, and NLP demonstrates KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but known limitations remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, robustness, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the right form of teacher knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational or contrastive signals) and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and targeted objectives; therefore KD should be treated as a first-line tool that must be adapted to the deployment context rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains compact student models to mimic larger teachers so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, practitioners match teacher output distributions, align intermediate representations, synthesize or filter data for student training, and combine distillation with structural compression (pruning, architecture search) to reach deployment targets. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher accuracy and sometimes improve generalization, but outcomes depend on the distillation signal, data provenance, student capacity, and training protocol. Practical deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to present supervision, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—has proven effective across vision, language, and other modalities. Practical success depends on co-designing what is transferred, student architecture and capacity, and data strategies; important open problems include robust transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, data-free and privacy-sensitive distillation, and principled combinations of KD with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and broadly applicable technique to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Work across computer vision, speech, and natural language processing demonstrates that KD can enable deployment of resource-efficient models, improve generalization in constrained settings, and be combined with other compression methods (e.g., low-precision numerics). At the same time, the field has identified important limitations and nuanced behaviors — such as data simplification effects, teacher–student mismatches, and domain or task-specific failure modes — that guide how KD should be applied in practice. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, variants, empirical benefits, and practical considerations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains in memory and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance, and it naturally extends beyond logits to include intermediate representations, attention maps, and synthesized inputs. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and transfer of unwanted behaviors mean distillation must be treated as a design pattern within a broader compression pipeline. When combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization, KD reliably supports real-world deployment while demanding careful, task-aware choices to avoid failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logit-matching for model compression into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, attention- and channel-level transfers, teacher ensembles, data- and teacher-free variants, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Practical success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment (capacity and architecture), the availability and provenance of data, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). While KD often preserves much of the teacher’s performance and can improve generalization through soft-target regularization, important limits remain around distribution shift, low-frequency token or class handling, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi-strategy toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision and natural language processing. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) and are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful choice of distilled signals and training schedules; remaining challenges include data-free distillation, heterogeneity between architectures, robustness and fairness under compression, and preservation of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD provides multiple channels of transferable information (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) that, when combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data synthesis), produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals and data, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Representation-aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, attention- or layer-aware mappings, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-conscious strategies—KD yields compact models that better preserve teacher behavior while meeting deployment constraints. However, realizing those benefits requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, and data constraints; KD is powerful but not a universal remedy.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical toolkit for turning large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Methods vary from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, optimization choices, and targeted handling of robustness, low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive settings. Important open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, preserving rare-token and domain-specific signals, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers or data are scarce, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that the students retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when original data are unavailable, and deploying progressive or ensemble-based strategies. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search) and training-time strategies (curricula, online distillation, or federated protocols) to balance efficiency and accuracy. Despite strong empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and designing principled objectives and curricula that preserve robustness and task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large deep models into compact ones that are suitable for deployment. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and specialized tasks such as machine reading comprehension, KD enables students to inherit performance-critical behaviors from larger teachers while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in model size and compute. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture search or structured pruning) and when tailored to task or domain specifics, distillation yields compressed models that approach teacher performance while meeting resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational alignment—consistently enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while recovering much of teacher accuracy when applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization dynamics. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distilled signals with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adopt data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols) to address real-world deployment challenges. Key open problems include robustly preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, handling distribution shift and privacy constraints, and automating student design for strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, expressive models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logit-matching to a diverse toolkit that includes feature- and layer-level supervision, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, self-distillation and teacher optimization, and approaches that enable data-free or privacy-preserving compression. Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling faster inference and smaller footprints; however, practical success depends on choices about objectives, alignment between teacher and student, data availability, and robustness to domain shift. Open directions include stronger theoretical characterization of what is transferred, principled treatment of heterogeneous teachers, and tighter integration of KD with quantization, pruning, and privacy mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. When treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single loss, KD supports a range of transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps), training regimes (single- and multi-teacher, online, data-free), and integrations with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, access to appropriate data (or metadata), and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Best practice treats distillation as part of an end-to-end compression pipeline that explicitly addresses alignment, data constraints, and downstream task objectives.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing high-capacity deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD methods span soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate representation and attention matching, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free training. Combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization, distillation enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy for real-world NLP deployments. However, success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, and strategies for handling domain shift, rare-token fidelity, and data- or privacy-constrained settings. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, practical core of compression pipelines and offers concrete recommendations and caveats for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, first‑line strategy for compressing large deep models for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible transfer channels (soft targets, intermediate features, attention and relational signals) that, when combined with architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, search), yield compact students that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity and alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and careful optimization and evaluation under distribution shift, fairness, and privacy constraints. Practitioners should adopt KD as a toolbox—selecting signals and curricula, aligning representations, and composing KD with other compression methods—while tracking open problems in theoretical guarantees, data-free and private distillation, and robust transfer of rare or domain‑specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central and practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in both deep learning and natural language processing. KD unifies a range of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and layer-wise objectives, and multi-teacher or data-free variants—and is typically integrated with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The effectiveness of KD depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data; when designed as part of a system-level pipeline KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs but faces open challenges in robustness, domain shift, privacy, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied model compression technique that trains a compact student model to emulate a larger teacher (or ensemble) so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD has been adapted across domains (vision, graphs, NLP, multimodal systems) and combined with other compression methods; it can transfer logits, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge, and it can be extended to multi-teacher, self-distillation, and privacy-aware settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves generalization but also reveals limits and failure modes that motivate augmented objectives, data strategies, and teacher-training methods to achieve more effective, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective strategy for compressing large models into efficient students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains. Beyond simply matching teacher logits, modern KD benefits from teaching intermediate representations, mimicking teacher features, self-distillation, and careful handling of multiple or stronger teachers. KD also composes well with structured pruning and other compression techniques to meet hardware constraints. This article synthesizes empirical lessons and recommended practices for applying KD reliably in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices for what and how to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), and when combined with complementary compression strategies (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Practical compression pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core tool whose design must be tailored to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Questions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses techniques that transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students). Across computer vision and natural language tasks, KD has been applied as logit-level supervision, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, self-distillation, domain-adaptive compression, and data-free/privacypreserving variants. Empirical work shows that distilled students can approach teacher performance while improving latency and footprint, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data complexity, and whether distillation occurs at the logits or feature level. Recent analyses link KD to label smoothing and show promising teacher-free or self-distillation approaches, while practical applications demonstrate domain-specific adaptation, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, and techniques to mitigate degenerate behaviours in sequence generation. Remaining challenges include handling domain shift, preserving low-frequency lexical details, training without original data, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide effective ways to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches span soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and data-free techniques, and multi-teacher or teacher-optimization strategies. Recent work emphasizes task-aware alignment between teacher and student representations, augmentation schemes that improve teacher-student consistency, and training teachers that are explicitly optimized to help downstream students, enabling more reliable deployment in low-resource and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the last decade a diverse toolkit has emerged — soft targets, intermediate representation and attention matching, layer-wise alignments, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, online/self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants — which practitioners combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical results show distillation often preserves much of teacher performance across modalities when objectives and data strategies are matched to student capacity; persistent challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, avoiding transfer of harmful biases, and building predictive theory about when distillation will succeed.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven approach for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while preserving much of task performance. KD methods—ranging from soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online variants, and data-free techniques—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has well-documented failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors, optimization mismatch) that require careful teacher/student design, data strategies, and complementary methods to get reliable results in practice.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi-Strategy Path for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for producing compact models that preserve much of larger models' performance. When treated as a flexible toolkit—integrating soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or low-precision numerics—KD enables deployable, efficient models across domains. KD is empirically effective but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or encountering optimization limits; best results arise from task- and data-aware distillation regimes and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential and Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but its reliability depends on choices about what to distill, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited, heterogeneous, or private data. Realistic deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, adapting the distillation signal to the task and student capacity, and evaluating robustness and privacy implications.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students retain much of the teachers’ functionality while being cheaper to run. KD operates through multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation). In practice KD is most effective when treated as a system-level pipeline that reconciles teacher–student mismatches, leverages appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized), and combines with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). The method reliably improves deployment trade-offs in many settings, but its success is context-dependent: it is sensitive to teacher quality and alignment, data availability and provenance, student capacity, and distributional or privacy constraints. Open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A spectrum of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational patterns) and training regimes (offline teacher-to-student, online co-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis) enables practical trade-offs between performance, latency, and memory. Effective compression usually combines distillation with architecture-aware choices and complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability; remaining challenges include distribution shift, preserving rare-token and domain-specific behavior, privacy-aware distillation, and reducing the computational cost of distillation itself.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that meet deployment constraints in compute, memory, latency, and privacy. When integrated with complementary techniques (layer mapping, data strategies, adversarial training, and architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss across vision and language tasks. Realizing these gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be a first-line strategy in compression pipelines while outlining practical caveats and design recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a central, practical toolkit for compressing large models and transferring behavior from high-capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative modeling, practitioners combine soft-label supervision, intermediate-representation matching, data- and privacy-aware strategies, and architecture-aware choices to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. KD is effective when paired with complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, synthetic-data generation, curriculum schedules), but its success depends critically on what form of knowledge is distilled, how data or augmentations are used, and how teacher–student capacity and domain mismatches are managed. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, mitigating bias transfer, and firm theoretical characterizations that predict when and how distillation will work in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD consistently reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when its objectives, teacher–student alignment, and data workflows are chosen deliberately. KD functions best as a system-level primitive that composes with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, but it is not a turnkey solution: effective and reliable deployment requires careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including data-free or privacy-sensitive regimes), and evaluation of robustness and domain-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks. The literature frames KD as a family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational and task-aware losses—combined with varied training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation, multi-teacher) and deployment-aware integrations (pretraining, architecture-aware adapters, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Empirical and theoretical studies show KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance while reducing parameter count and latency, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the choice of what and how to transfer. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, handling heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or domain-specific signals, and reducing the computational cost of distillation itself.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is matched to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch. When designers select what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to expose the student to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online peer predictions), and how to adapt protocols for distributed or privacy-sensitive settings, KD yields large practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability while controlling risks such as bias transfer or robustness loss. A deployment-aware KD practice leverages representation-aware objectives, data-free synthesis when training data are unavailable, adversarial or online schemes for richer alignment, and federated-distillation architectures for communication-efficient collaboration.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide a set of complementary strategies to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models. Methods span matching output distributions (soft targets), imitating intermediate representations and attention, aligning layers, using multiple teachers or self-teaching schedules, and applying task- or data-aware procedures including data-free generation and low-precision adaptation. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance while gaining speed and memory efficiency, but outcomes depend on which knowledge is transferred, student capacity, data availability, and task specificity. Practical deployments combine distillation with architecture search, quantization, and curriculum or augmentation strategies to balance fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, data-free or few-shot protocols). Practical outcomes depend on teacher quality and specialization, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability; open problems include reliable transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and operating under privacy or data-limited constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in constrained environments. Advances across task-adaptive compression, data-free and zero-shot distillation, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and self-distillation demonstrate KD's broad applicability. However, KD is not a panacea: success depends on data availability, the teacher–student optimization dynamics, and explicit design choices around architecture and training signals. Combining pre-training of compact models, task-aware architecture search, and sophisticated distillation protocols yields the best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance characteristics from larger models. Research has introduced multiple KD paradigms—teacher-student soft-label transfer, self-distillation, feature/internal-representation matching, multi-teacher strategies, and data-augmentation–aware distillation—each addressing different practical constraints such as domain shift, resource limits, or heterogeneous architectures. Applications span speech, machine translation evaluation, ASR, and domain-specific pretrained models; empirical work shows substantial reductions in model size and latency can be achieved with modest accuracy loss, or sometimes even gains, when distillation is combined with architectural adaptations and training-time strategies. Remaining challenges include transferring internal representations across heterogeneous architectures, choosing or designing teachers that are most useful for particular students, and preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals during aggressive compression.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data strategies, and optimization choices are carefully managed. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and fairness under compression, and operating under limited or no access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Core, Methods, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for converting large pretrained models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. When applied with attention to what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned (architecture-aware objectives, projectors, layer selection), and how data constraints are handled (data augmentation, data-free synthesis, privacy-aware workflows), KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across NLP and multimodal tasks. Nevertheless, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and robustness under distribution shift, so practitioners should pair KD with complementary compression tools and task-aware evaluations to deploy compact models reliably.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their predictive power. Nonetheless, its effectiveness depends strongly on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including few-shot or data-free regimes), and the choice of distilled signals; recognizing these dependencies leads to principled best practices that balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.title: Make Knowledge Distillation the Core of Compression Pipelines — With Careful Complementary Design
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, first-line strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD offers a flexible toolkit that can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, and relational signals, and it integrates naturally with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, data-free synthesis). However, KD is not a turnkey solution: success requires deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, alignment of teacher and student capacity and architecture, data availability and provenance, and safeguards for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy. Combining KD with targeted complementary methods and data-aware practices yields the best practical accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

However, distillation outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the form of distilled knowledge (logits, features, attention), access to data, and optimization choices. Best results arise when distillation is integrated with appropriate pre-training, architectural adapters (projectors or attention alignment), and, when necessary, data synthesis or domain adaptation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges

However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on careful method selection, complementary compression steps, and mitigation of teacher–student mismatch and data limitations.
