papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label transfers to a rich family of techniques including internal representation matching, attention- and channel-guided supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble signals, data-free and augmentation-driven methods, and architecture-aware transformations. Practical deployments combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search and must balance transfer of useful teacher information against risks such as propagating teacher errors or overfitting under limited data. The field continues to refine what teacher knowledge to transfer, how to synthesize or augment training data when it is unavailable, and how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures for robust, resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language. A diverse set of distillation recipes—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, self- and online-distillation, ensemble-to-single transfer, and data-free synthesis—enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy. Success depends on co-designing teacher and student architectures, selecting appropriate transfer signals, handling data availability or privacy constraints, and integrating complementary compression methods. Remaining gaps include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, and principled theory to predict when particular distillation strategies will succeed in production.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of model-compression techniques that trains smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior from larger teacher models. Across vision and language tasks, KD methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include alignment of internal representations, attention or relational signals, adversarially-informed objectives, online or multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies. Effective application balances what is transferred, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and robustness or fairness constraints, and it is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants—has been developed to meet deployment constraints in vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows that, when combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though careful method selection is required to mitigate mismatches, data limitations, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD operates at multiple levels — softened output distributions, intermediate feature or attention imitation, and relational or layer-wise alignment — and composes naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy for deployed systems, but its success depends on careful design choices related to what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Practical deployment treats KD as a core element of a hybrid compression pipeline, with task-aware signal selection, student-aware teacher design, and targeted remedies for distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, adversarial vulnerability, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models so the students can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a broad family of objectives that include intermediate representation matching, attention- and relational-level transfer, ensemble-to-single distillation, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. In practice KD is most effective when its signals are chosen to match student capacity and the deployment setting, and when it is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data strategies. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior (especially in NLP), aligning heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as a central, system-level approach to model compression and adaptation. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger teachers to smaller students, KD enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world success depends on co-designing teacher and student, selecting what signals to transfer, combining distillation with complementary compression techniques, and using data strategies (including data-free or few-shot protocols) to handle privacy- or data-limited settings. When applied thoughtfully, KD serves as a unifying, practical toolkit for creating efficient, deployable models across modalities; however, careful mitigation of teacher-induced biases, distribution shift, and robustness issues is required.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable smaller or faster models to retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific inductive biases. Work in this area spans supervised soft-target matching, intermediate-layer representation transfer, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, and online/distributed variants that exploit parallelism. Applications include compressing large pretrained language models for downstream NLP tasks, accelerating inference for computer vision and generative models, and producing interpretable or privacy-preserving compact models for healthcare and on-device deployment. Important trade-offs involve what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, activations, relations), access to training data, robustness to domain heterogeneity, and how to balance capacity, efficiency, and generalization in student models.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded toolkit that enables compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when paired with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods. However, its effectiveness is context-dependent: success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy concerns. Treating KD as the backbone of an integrated compression pipeline delivers the best practical outcomes while acknowledging and mitigating its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains compact student models to mimic larger teachers so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, practitioners match teacher output distributions, align intermediate representations, synthesize or filter data for student training, and combine distillation with structural compression (pruning, architecture search) to reach deployment targets. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher accuracy and sometimes improve generalization, but outcomes depend on the distillation signal, data provenance, student capacity, and training protocol. Practical deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to present supervision, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Patterns, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a rich toolkit that also includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free training strategies. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student co-design, KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of a teacher’s predictive power. Important practical challenges remain, including robust transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or domain-specific behavior (especially in NLP), and principled, privacy-aware distillation when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, System-Level Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD should be treated as the backbone of compression pipelines: when co-designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, it delivers most of the real-world gains in latency, memory, and deployability while exposing clear trade-offs and failure modes that must be managed.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically effective strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as the first-line compression method and combined with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies), KD enables deployable students across modalities while also serving as a regularizer that can improve generalization. However, KD has well-documented failure modes — teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, data-limited or privacy-constrained settings, and difficulties preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors — so practical deployment requires careful co-design of teacher signals, student capacity, and data protocols. The body of evidence supports KD as a central tool in compression pipelines but emphasizes hybrid workflows and targeted mitigations for its limits.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical, flexible, and widely applied approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and language tasks. KD brings together soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware strategies into a single, adaptable pipeline that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet real-world deployment constraints. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs, its reliability depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these concerns makes KD a central component of robust, system-level compression workflows rather than a one-shot recipe.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that meet deployment constraints in compute, memory, latency, and privacy. When integrated with complementary techniques (layer mapping, data strategies, adversarial training, and architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss across vision and language tasks. Realizing these gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be a first-line strategy in compression pipelines while outlining practical caveats and design recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students that retain much of the teachers' performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation-level objectives, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-free or zero-shot variants, and architecture-aware combinations with pruning, quantization, and search. KD has been applied successfully across domains — including language generation, ranking, detection, and federated settings — but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data, privacy, and distributional shift. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation signals and training regimes that match student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Mechanisms, and Responsible Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practically effective approach for producing compact models that can be deployed under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When treated as a flexible design paradigm rather than a single loss, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), integrates with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization), and adapts to task- and data-specific constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free or synthetic strategies), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behavior. A considered KD pipeline—combining softened logits, representational guidance, task-aware objectives, architecture-aware search, and careful data strategies—yields compact students that meet real-world deployment needs while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in constrained environments. Advances across task-adaptive compression, data-free and zero-shot distillation, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and self-distillation demonstrate KD's broad applicability. However, KD is not a panacea: success depends on data availability, the teacher–student optimization dynamics, and explicit design choices around architecture and training signals. Combining pre-training of compact models, task-aware architecture search, and sophisticated distillation protocols yields the best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for making large neural models deployable: by transferring richer supervision from high-capacity teacher models to compact students, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving or even improving generalization. Best results arise when distillation strategies are matched to deployment constraints and student capacity—combining logits and representational objectives, co-designing teacher and student, using appropriate data-augmentation or synthetic-data strategies, and integrating structural compression like pruning or module replacement. Although challenges remain (teacher imperfections, low-frequency token fidelity, data-free settings, and distribution shift), a set of practical, complementary methods yields robust pathways to efficient models across NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring useful information from large teacher models to smaller students. Methods span soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, and data-free or zero‑shot synthesis to handle unavailable or private training data. KD is typically combined with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and training practices (curricula, augmentation) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Despite strong empirical success across vision, speech, and NLP, important limitations remain: principled theory of when distillation helps, reliable transfer of robustness and fairness, handling distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena, and automated student design for specific resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teachers. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), how teachers are chosen or ensembled, and whether distillation is done with or without access to original data. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data augmentation, or synthetic-data generation) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, success depends on careful objective design, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as degraded handling of low‑frequency tokens, adversarial vulnerability, or erased relative class information.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD spans soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, layer-aware alignment, self-distillation, and architecture-replacement strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture changes), KD enables practical tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, and memory for NLP and other modalities. Effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, what form of knowledge is transferred, and constraints such as data availability, privacy, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance, self-distillation, and curriculum or task-aware schedules — has been developed and validated across vision, language, and domain-specific tasks. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, leveraging data or synthetic-data strategies when needed, and combining KD with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Important open challenges include transferring rare-token or long-tail behavior, preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift, and automating student design for target resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Work across vision and language shows a set of recurring strategies: transfer using softened outputs (soft targets), imitation of intermediate/internal representations, layer mapping between teacher and student, task-adaptive architecture search, self-distillation, and data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable. Empirical results indicate that properly designed distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while offering large gains in inference speed and memory; however, success depends on which knowledge is transferred (outputs vs. internal features), how layers are aligned, and whether task specificity and data availability are addressed. The field currently balances practical engineering (architecture and search) with algorithmic refinements (losses and training regimes), and open challenges include robust data-free methods, principled many-to-many layer matching, and teacher designs that are optimized to be “student-friendly.”

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deploying compact models that retain much of teacher performance, supports cross-modal and task-specific transfers, and can be adapted to privacy- and data-constrained settings. While highly effective in practice, KD’s outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design; realizing its full potential requires targeted methodological choices such as feature-level matching, multi-teacher fusion, adversarial data synthesis, and privacy-preserving mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes representation alignment, architecture-aware student design, and data strategies, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD’s benefits are context-sensitive: success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free regimes), and attention to robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy. To be effective in production, KD should be applied as a toolkit—combined with complementary methods and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Principled Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical technique for compressing large neural models into deployable, efficient students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, multi-task, and low-precision settings, distillation can recover large-model accuracy in smaller footprints when combined with careful design choices that address capacity mismatch, task relevance, and the nature of the transferred knowledge. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on distillation schedule, selection of what to transfer (logits, features, or task-aware subsets), and occasionally on teacher improvement or specialization. Understanding these interactions is key to robust compression for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. It encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- or module-level mappings, and training-time adaptations that account for student capacity and deployment constraints. In practice KD is combined with complementary methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis) to meet latency, memory, or privacy requirements. KD is effective across vision, language, generative models, and view- or modality-specific tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, available data, and careful choice of distillation objectives and schedules; open challenges remain in robustness, rare-token behavior, fairness, and theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD should be treated as a first‑line strategy: it reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with capacity-aware student design, appropriate distilled signals, and complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure — its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks — so practitioners must apply KD as part of an integrated compression pipeline and evaluate its trade-offs in realistic deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable route to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive capability. KD achieves favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities and tasks, but its real-world success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and deployment constraints. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a core tool that should routinely be combined with complementary compression, data, and training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining as much task performance as possible. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a broad set of practical techniques that include intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, online and multi-teacher training, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially shrink model size and latency for vision and language systems and can be adapted for privacy-sensitive and distributed settings; however, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data, and it faces open challenges in robustness, cross-domain generalization, and heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains smaller student models to capture the behavior of larger teacher models, enabling deployment under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy while often preserving much of teacher performance. Its practical effectiveness arises from multiple complementary mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation transfer, and data or architecture adaptations) and from combining distillation with structural compression techniques. However, distillation’s success is contingent on choices about teacher–student pairing, the provenance and availability of data, the distilled signals and training schedules, and deployment constraints such as federated or privacy-sensitive settings. A principled, task-aware approach that blends appropriate distillation objectives, data strategies (including data-free methods when necessary), and complementary compression methods yields the best tradeoffs between compactness and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has developed a broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and feature-level transfer, multi‑teacher and online schemes, and data‑free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data strategies, and optimization choices are carefully managed. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and fairness under compression, and operating under limited or no access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and projector-based transforms, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search) and careful teacher–student design, KD routinely yields substantial inference and memory savings while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical application requires attention to teacher quality, data availability, capacity and architecture mismatch, and task-specific objectives (e.g., robustness or privacy); addressing these issues motivates specialized distillation losses, student-aware teacher training, data synthesis, and adversarial or privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers real efficiency gains when its targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and training protocols are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its best use is as the central element of a compression pipeline that explicitly addresses teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success requires careful design of distilled signals, data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical Core That Requires Contextual Integration
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly practical and widely used approach for producing compact models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. Empirical evidence shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, and it has been extended from simple soft-target supervision to feature-level, attention, and data-synthesis variants. However, KD’s reliability and adequacy in production depend on choices about what to distill, teacher–student alignment, data availability and domain shift, and fairness and privacy concerns. Consequently, KD functions best as a central element within a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, complementary compression (pruning, quantization), targeted data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness and bias.

papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line, Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from soft outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment practices. While KD should be treated as a primary strategy in compression pipelines because of its empirical utility and adaptability, its reliable use requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data provenance or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with architectural or numerical compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data availability, and optimization dynamics are considered; however, its success is contingent on capacity alignment, data choices, and safeguards against transferring undesirable behaviors. Applications range from accelerated inference and edge deployment to domain adaptation, federated learning, and task-specific adaptations such as non-autoregressive translation and graph-to-MLP compression.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including domain adaptation and black-box/data-free workflows). In practice KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures, combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and tailored to data availability and deployment constraints. Despite wide empirical success across vision and NLP, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, distilling rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable compression when training data are limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD mechanisms — soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and task- or deployment-aware pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in inference cost, but success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and task-specific considerations (e.g., preserving fine-grained sequence behavior or relational structure). Privacy, heterogeneity of deployment devices, and data-scarce regimes motivate variants with differential privacy, few-shot or cross-layer schemes, and heterogeneous multi-model sharing to ensure inclusive and practical compression.

When combined with task-aware design, multi-teacher curricula, and safeguards for fairness and privacy, KD yields compact models that meet real-world production requirements while preserving most of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a primary, flexible strategy for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD supports a wide range of supervision signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses), training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, adversarial, data-free), and combinations with structural compression (pruning, quantization) or architecture search. When applied with task- and student-aware design choices, KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs; however, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, capacity alignment, and careful selection of what to transfer. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as the backbone of compression while integrating complementary methods and safeguards to address gaps in robustness, privacy, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, privacy, or device constraints. KD methods operate across multiple knowledge channels (soft logits, internal features, attention/relations, layer mappings), and they are often combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis). Empirical work shows distilled students can often recover the bulk of teacher performance while reducing compute and memory substantially, but effectiveness depends on task, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional shifts. Important open problems remain in data-free distillation, few-shot compression, preserving rare-token behaviors and robustness, and designing distillation as a system-level primitive matched to deployment constraints.

Remaining gaps include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, and principled theory to predict when particular distillation strategies will succeed in production.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Deployment Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) occupies a central, practical role in compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision and language applications. KD offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that—when deliberately chosen and combined with complementary compression methods—regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is context dependent: its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability and augmentation, the choice of distilled signals, and explicit checks for robustness and rare-case behavior. I argue KD should be the first-line tool in a compression pipeline but must be used together with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and targeted evaluation to avoid common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multi-Strategy, Practical Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive power while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Best results arise when distillation is combined with complementary techniques — representation matching, ensembling, architecture-aware compression, pretraining of compact students, and data-aware strategies — and when practitioners account for deployment-specific mismatches (domain shift, heterogeneous inputs, or limited access to data). Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rare or low-frequency information, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and designing data-free or privacy-preserving distillation that reliably generalizes under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical and versatile approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or synthetic data to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with task-aware design, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and appropriate input-side strategies, distillation supports robust deployment across NLP and other modalities. Nevertheless, careful design is required to manage teacher–student mismatch, preserve low-frequency or domain-specific signals, and operate when original training data is limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably yields compact models that retain much of a larger teacher’s performance when applied with attention to what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability. KD works through multiple mechanisms—soft-target regularization, representation transfer, and ensemble-derived ‘‘dark knowledge’’—and its strengths are maximized when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware training curricula. However, KD is not a universal solution: practical deployments must address limits including distribution shift, rare-token behavior, privacy-sensitive or data-free scenarios, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher behavior. I therefore argue that KD should be treated as the practical core of hybrid compression pipelines, selected and tuned according to deployment constraints and supplemented with methods that mitigate its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effective, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates via multiple knowledge channels — softened logits, intermediate feature matching, attention or relational signals, and ensemble or multi-teacher supervision — and it composes well with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architectural replacement). Empirical results across vision, speech, and NLP show that carefully chosen distillation targets, student pre-training, data augmentation, and multi-teacher strategies reliably improve deployment trade-offs, but KD’s success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and domain heterogeneity. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible pipeline: design the student and distillation targets for the task and capacity of the student, use multi-source or ensemble teachers when appropriate, apply representation projection to reconcile mismatches, and explicitly evaluate under realistic data heterogeneity or deployment constraints to avoid hidden failures.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach that compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across modalities (NLP, speech, vision) and tasks. Its practical success depends on the choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and teacher-student design; when combined with augmentation, ensemble guidance, or privacy-aware mechanisms, KD supports real-world deployment while requiring safeguards against bias, privacy leakage, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language applications. As a flexible toolkit, KD encompasses multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), modes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (real, augmented, synthetic, data-free, privacy-aware). When combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. The effectiveness of distillation depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability and match of training data; persistent challenges include preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, avoiding transfer of undesirable properties, and robust distillation under distribution shift or data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance characteristics from larger models. Research has introduced multiple KD paradigms—teacher-student soft-label transfer, self-distillation, feature/internal-representation matching, multi-teacher strategies, and data-augmentation–aware distillation—each addressing different practical constraints such as domain shift, resource limits, or heterogeneous architectures. Applications span speech, machine translation evaluation, ASR, and domain-specific pretrained models; empirical work shows substantial reductions in model size and latency can be achieved with modest accuracy loss, or sometimes even gains, when distillation is combined with architectural adaptations and training-time strategies. Remaining challenges include transferring internal representations across heterogeneous architectures, choosing or designing teachers that are most useful for particular students, and preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals during aggressive compression.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Focused Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for producing compact models by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students. Methods extend beyond matching softened output distributions to include intermediate-feature imitation, attention or relational alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or synthetic-data procedures. Best practices combine representation-aware objectives, student-aware architecture choices, and data strategies (pretraining, augmentation, or synthetic data) and often pair KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work across vision, speech, and NLP demonstrates KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but known limitations remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, robustness, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models while attempting to preserve accuracy and useful inductive biases. Approaches span classic teacher–student logit matching, representation and feature imitation, layer mapping strategies for large pretrained language models, data-free and zero-shot methods that avoid access to original training data, and privacy- or communication-aware frameworks for distributed settings. Empirical work demonstrates these methods can yield practical speedups, substantial parameter reductions, and competitive task performance across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks; theoretical and empirical studies also clarify when softened teacher targets or distilled datasets best help student capacity. Remaining challenges include balancing privacy and utility, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers are large, and extending guarantees and methods across modalities and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical backbone of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible toolkit to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers to compact students, enabling large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy — its success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data methods), and complementary compression steps; production-grade deployment therefore requires disciplined evaluation of robustness, fairness, and task-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression: Effectiveness, Limits, and Practical Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When treated as a system—choosing which signals to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning teacher and student architectures, managing data and sample selection, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks. Its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and attention to robustness and rare-token behavior; hence KD is best used as the central element of a broader compression pipeline rather than as a standalone fix.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and pragmatic framework for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private models across modalities and tasks. When applied thoughtfully — by matching outputs, intermediate representations, training dynamics, or ensembles — KD can preserve or even improve task performance while enabling low-latency inference, reduced memory/compute, and new deployment modes (e.g., federated, data-free, or low-precision). However, distillation is not automatic: design choices about what to transfer, when to transfer, and how to align teacher and student matter for robustness, domain shifts, and rare-token behavior. I argue that best practice combines representation-aware objectives, selective or collaborative teaching strategies, and deployment-aware constraints (privacy, communication, numeric precision) to realize the full benefits of distillation in NLP and other deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving predictive performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, contrastive and relational signals, online or teacher-free co-training, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data availability; remaining challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and reliable distillation when original data are limited or private.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Favoring Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, versatile pathway to produce compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a design paradigm—choosing what form of knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs across modalities. KD should be adopted as the default first‑line compression method in deep learning and NLP while being applied with careful safeguards for data, robustness, and task alignment.
