papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD succeeds across modalities when treated as a design pipeline that combines what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints and deployment constraints (privacy, latency, heterogeneity). KD is powerful but not universally sufficient: realizing its benefits requires co-design of teacher and student, complementary compression techniques, and safeguards for low-frequency phenomena, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural networks for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Beyond simple model-size reduction, KD enables transfer of inductive biases, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving distributed training, data-free and zero-shot compression, and the transfer of adversarial robustness. Combining logit-based distillation with feature-level mimicking and carefully chosen regularization yields high-quality small models that remain competitive on downstream tasks in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Methods and Challenges in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across vision, generative modeling, and NLP, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, task-specific adaptations, multi-teacher schemes, and teacher-optimization strategies to improve student accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. Work also focuses on constraints arising in distributed and privacy-preserving settings, on preserving rare or fine-grained information, and on adapting distillation to complex tasks such as detection, generation, and dense prediction. Practical systems combine architectural choices, training curricula, and distilled supervision to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. A rich toolbox has emerged—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with structural compression—that makes it possible to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, data availability, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and domain-specific behavior, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatch in heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers real efficiency gains when its targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and training protocols are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its best use is as the central element of a compression pipeline that explicitly addresses teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success requires careful design of distilled signals, data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques that transfers information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or feature distributions, and can be combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) or data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and provenance of data, and robustness to distributional shifts. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as one element of a broader compression toolkit and apply task- and deployment-aware design choices to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bradshaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer aspects of teacher behavior—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, availability of (or access to) data, and careful design of distillation objectives and training curricula. Open problems include robust transfer under domain shift, reliable data-free distillation, preservation of rare or safety-critical behaviors, and principled co-design of teacher and student for deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the last decade a diverse toolkit has emerged — soft targets, intermediate representation and attention matching, layer-wise alignments, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, online/self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants — which practitioners combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical results show distillation often preserves much of teacher performance across modalities when objectives and data strategies are matched to student capacity; persistent challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, avoiding transfer of harmful biases, and building predictive theory about when distillation will succeed.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A heterogeneous family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher schedules, data-free synthesis, and task- or architecture-aware adaptations—enables compact models to approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Effective application requires careful choice of distilled signals, attention to teacher–student capacity and data availability, and often combining distillation with complementary compression methods; limitations remain around optimization difficulties, distribution shift, privacy-sensitive scenarios, and reliably transferring robustness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate-feature alignment, attention and relational transfer, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Practical deployments typically combine KD with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies; remaining research challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving low-frequency or rare behaviors, privacy leakage, and principled automation of teacher/student design.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a family of methods that include feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and projection, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful design choices about which signals to transfer. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or undesirable behaviors. This synthesis summarizes common methods, mechanisms, practical patterns, and outstanding limitations to guide researchers and practitioners applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and other modalities. A broad family of techniques transfers different forms of teacher information — from softened logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data-free synthesis and adversarially guided generation). Empirical evidence shows that, when carefully designed to match teacher–student capacity and data conditions, KD can retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, mitigating bias transfer, and characterizing when particular distillation objectives succeed in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of teacher knowledge. Across vision and language tasks KD has enabled practical reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on what form of knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student representations are aligned, the availability and selection of data for distillation, and complementary compression techniques such as low-precision numerics, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent exact teacher matching, reliable distillation without original data, robustness and fairness under compression, and principled methods for matching heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compact, Robust Deep Models: Effectiveness, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD succeeds when its design (what to transfer, how, and with which data) is matched to deployment constraints: transferring logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals; using multi- or adaptive-teacher schedules; and combining distillation with model- and data-level compression. However, KD is not a panacea — optimization gaps, mismatched inputs or teachers, and inappropriate sample selection can degrade results — so robust application requires careful teacher-student co-design, selective supervision, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple logit matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data- and communication-constrained protocols, and progressive module replacement. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and training protocols. Important open issues include robust transfer under distribution shift, efficient distillation when teacher cost is high, and preserving fairness and safety properties in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—logit matching, feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student schemes, and hybrid pipelines combined with pruning or architecture modification—that make it adaptable to diverse deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When applied with attention to the form of transferred knowledge, teacher quality, and data strategies, KD yields compact models suitable for production NLP and cross-modal systems; however, careful design is required to avoid pitfalls such as degraded calibration, transferred biases, or student–teacher mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. Over the past decade KD has diversified from soft-label (logit) matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, attention and relational supervision, contrastive and projector-based objectives, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture co-design) and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in inference cost with modest losses in task performance. Realizing these benefits in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and availability, and evaluation for robustness and fairness; several open problems remain, notably reliable data-free distillation, principled teacher design, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying deep models under resource constraints. Methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-layer supervision, feature mimicking, projector-based transforms, teacher-student co-training, and data- or domain-aware schemes. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs) and in settings with limited or no access to original training data. Practical advances address transfer across architectures, task-adaptive compression, and efficient architecture search, while open problems remain around distribution shift, heterogeneity of data or detectors, and preserving rare or low-frequency information.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) uses larger or ensemble teacher models to train smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s predictive ability while reducing inference cost. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened outputs to include intermediate representation matching, layer- and channel-wise guidance, ensemble and multi-teacher approaches, self-distillation, data-free and federated variants, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates substantial size and latency reductions across vision and NLP with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully chosen and paired with appropriate data or synthesis strategies. Remaining practical and scientific challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, operating without original training data, mitigating transferred biases, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student capacities.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. A spectrum of KD strategies has been developed—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, self-distillation, and data-free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows well-designed distillation pipelines can recover much of a teacher’s performance while delivering large gains in latency and memory, but outcomes depend on the choice of distillation signal, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints such as domain shift and privacy. Current practical directions emphasize representation-aware objectives, layer-alignment techniques, and hybrid pipelines that treat KD as a core element of system-level compression.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques reliably reduce large pretrained models to compact, efficient students suitable for deployment while preserving most of the teacher performance. Across NLP and multimodal tasks, practical compression requires strategies that (1) align representations at multiple levels, (2) focus on task-relevant information, and (3) handle limited or no access to original training data. Combining architecture-aware search, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, and improved input-side strategies (including data augmentation or data-free sample generation) yields compact models with strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs suitable for real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. A spectrum of KD techniques—from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher supervision, and architecture-aware student design—has been shown to recover much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical success depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and alignment between teacher and student; practical systems also require attention to computational cost during distillation and to domain or heterogeneity challenges in distributed settings. Remaining gaps include principled selection of teacher signals for specific tasks, reliable data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and methods that scale distillation quality and efficiency simultaneously.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically supported path to compress large models into compact, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central design pattern rather than a single loss term, KD enables multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and online schedules, and integration with architecture-aware design and other compression methods. Practical success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including pre-training of compact architectures and data augmentation or synthesis), and theoretical understanding of when soft versus hard supervision helps. Framed this way, KD is the most practical, multi-strategy mechanism for real-world compression, provided practitioners pair it with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.
